operator_plays.name: Forced-Pooling Docket & Non-Consent Mineral Lease Curve-Jumping Arbitrage
operator_plays.mechanism: Use public pooling applications and drilling schedules to identify unleased mineral interests before election deadlines, pricing royalty upside against title defects and non-consent cost exposure.

Mineral ownership chain and lease abstracts
Operator development plans and local lease comparables
workflow: 1. Monitor pooling applications and map affected mineral tracts and hearing dates
2. Verify net mineral acres, ownership authority, and election consequences with specialist counsel
3. Negotiate disclosed lease or option terms and fund obligations before applicable deadlines
4. Assign permitted interests or administer royalty receipts with division-order reconciliation

positioning_alternatives.title: The Title-First Royalty Acquisition Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Underwrite producing oil and gas mineral interests through recorded ownership, lease economics, and reconciled royalty receipts.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Capital-backed owner-operators building a four-person acquisition pod around producing mineral interests and nonparticipating royalties.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: Texas Property Code Sections 5.021 and 13.001 make conveyance formalities and recording consequences central diligence questions. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 supplies payment timing rules and specified grounds for withholding proceeds. These sources support an evidence-led acquisition process, not a valuation shortcut.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Pooling-Docket Acquisition Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Price acreage before public development milestones resolve, without treating a pooling application as a producing well.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Basin-specialist buyers pairing a landman and petroleum engineer with patient acquisition capital and disciplined docket monitoring.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: State commission records establish the applicable pooling process, case status, and development evidence. Texas Natural Resources Code Chapter 102 governs a specific statutory pooling mechanism; it is not interchangeable with Oklahoma Corporation Commission practice. A filed application, issued order, permit, completed well, and paid royalty are separate underwriting events.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Institutional Mineral Exit Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Assemble auditable title and production packages, then recognize rights-sale gains separately from returned acquisition basis.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Experienced mineral buyers preparing institution-ready assets, with a six-person expansion reserved for demonstrated deal volume.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 15 U.S.C. Section 77b includes fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within the securities definition. Section 77e establishes registration requirements, subject to applicable exemptions. 26 U.S.C. Sections 611 and 613A make depletion treatment a separate asset-specific tax analysis rather than an automatic deduction from every sale or royalty payment.

chapters.question_prompt: What exactly is mineral rights, how is real operator revenue recognized vs underlying asset/client GMV, and what separates durable small-team moats from fragile beginner hype?
chapters.title: What Exactly Is Mineral Rights?
chapters.subtitle: Underwrite NMA, NPRI, Oklahoma Pooling Elections, Texas Royalty Payments, and Institutional Mineral Exits
chapters.executive_summary: Mineral rights converts documented subsurface ownership into royalty receipts and realized rights-trading gains, not credit for an operator's entire production stream. Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: capital and specialized labor matter more than acquisition volume. Five mapped plays anchor this chapter: forced-pooling docket curve-jumping, producing-royalty acquisition, NPRI specialization, unleased-mineral lease-up, and institutional portfolio assembly. Canonical annual owner profits are $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled. The durable business pairs tract-level title evidence with payment reconciliation, disciplined depletion models, and executable exits. Start with $15,000–$75,000 of capital, budget a 6–24 month first-deal cycle, and refuse acreage whose ownership fraction, payment formula, or election exposure cannot be independently established.

sections.heading: 1. Buy the Ownership Formula, Not the Acreage Headline
paragraphs: Mineral rights is the business of acquiring, leasing, holding, and transferring legally defined interests in subsurface resources. This volume focuses on United States oil and gas, where the mineral estate can be severed from surface ownership and divided again by substance, depth, formation, geography, and time. A mineral interest may carry leasing authority and rights to bonuses, rentals, and royalties, but the actual conveyance determines which sticks remain. A nonparticipating royalty interest, or NPRI, generally receives a specified royalty share without executive leasing rights; bonus and rental participation require separate document analysis. An overriding royalty comes out of a leasehold interest and ordinarily depends on that lease surviving. A working interest bears operating obligations and is not interchangeable with a passive royalty. Buying the surface alone proves none of these interests exists in the seller. The small-team operator therefore purchases a documented payment formula attached to identified land, not a promotional count of nearby rigs. Begin every opportunity with the deed, legal description, ownership fraction, reservations, lease status, and evidence connecting that interest to the well or unit expected to pay. A county map pin is a research lead, never an ownership certificate.

Net mineral acres, or NMA, express tract acreage multiplied by the owned mineral fraction. Twenty gross acres owned at one-half equal ten NMA. If those ten NMA participate uniformly in a 640-acre unit under a 20% lease royalty, the simplified revenue decimal is 10 divided by 640 times 0.20, or 0.003125. Applied to $1,000,000 of applicable unit sales, that produces $3,125 before taxes, permitted deductions, and adjustments. The million dollars belongs to the production context; it is not the mineral buyer's revenue. Actual allocation can differ because of tract participation, lateral allocation, depth limitations, or unit terms. NPRI wording requires another calculation: a fixed 1/16 royalty is not necessarily the same interest as 1/16 of the lessor's royalty. On the same fully attributable $100,000 sales base, those alternatives produce $6,250 and, under a one-quarter lease royalty, $1,562.50 respectively. Obtain a document-specific interpretation before pricing either. Net royalty acre conventions also vary, including normalization to a one-eighth royalty; require every seller and buyer to state the conversion explicitly. Never reconcile two acreage quotations until their economic denominators and depth coverage are identical.

Five operator archetypes organize the opportunity rather than promising five independent sources of effortless income. Forced-pooling docket curve-jumping buys accurately understood interests while a public proceeding changes the development timetable. Producing-royalty acquisition purchases an existing payment stream whose decline and deductions can be measured. NPRI specialization resolves fractional language and executive-rights dependencies that generalist buyers often price poorly. Unleased-mineral lease-up converts verified leasing authority into a negotiated lease and eventual royalty exposure. Institutional portfolio assembly standardizes numerous small interests into a package that a larger buyer can underwrite efficiently. The first four can supply inventory to the fifth, but selling a portfolio is an exit, not a second claim on revenue already booked. Assign one accountable principal, a contract land professional, mineral counsel, and a royalty accountant before scaling. The canonical Conservative and Base teams are one full-time operator plus three contractors, not four full-time salaries. Scaled adds a second full-time operator and a fourth contractor for six people total. Contractor count does not establish hours or rates. Set scope-based budgets, keep acquisition capital separate from operating runway, and expect the initial transaction cycle to consume six to twenty-four months rather than treating published drilling activity as an immediate closing commitment.

callout.title: Four Habits That Separate Mineral Buyers from Acreage Collectors
callout.body: Earn speed through organized evidence, not through skipping document interpretation.
items: Put gross acres, mineral fraction, lease royalty, unit participation, and payment decimal on one worksheet; require every intermediate calculation to reconcile.
Compare three consecutive EnergyLink statements against production months rather than deposit dates; investigate changed decimals before projecting higher income.
Ask institutional buyers for depth limits, minimum package size, title standards, and recourse expectations before assembling their supposed ideal portfolio.
For every NPRI reservation, write both competing dollar outcomes before counsel resolves the language; ambiguity becomes visible when translated into cash.

sections.heading: 2. Select the Sub-Vertical Before Choosing the Purchase Multiple
paragraphs: A mineral portfolio is not one homogeneous yield instrument. A mature gas well, an undeveloped shale bench, a term royalty, and a leasehold override have different duration, operating dependencies, and exit buyers. Screen the sub-vertical before asking whether the price is cheap. Enverus and Novi Labs can support production and development comparisons, while state regulator records establish filed permits, well identifiers, and reported activity. Commercial subscriptions are research expenses, not proof that a development forecast will occur. EnergyNet provides a transaction channel, but listing terms, buyer charges, seller commissions, and settlement conditions must come from the actual engagement. Never invent a universal marketplace fee. County searches and CourthouseDirect can accelerate document retrieval without replacing a tract-specific title examination. EnergyLink supports statement access and reconciliation where the payer participates; its data does not cure a defective deed. Record each source's date, geographic coverage, and missing periods. A useful acquisition memorandum separates facts established by recorded instruments, operator representations, engineering assumptions, and the buyer's own valuation choices. That separation lets a second reviewer challenge a price without reopening every document or mistaking a vendor-generated forecast for a binding drilling obligation.

The mandatory play, forced_pooling_mineral_lease_curve_jumping, uses public pooling applications and drilling schedules to locate unleased interests before an applicable election deadline. Oklahoma's framework under 52 O.S. § 87.1 requires attention to the actual proceeding and order; an application alone does not establish the final election menu or deadline. Price the royalty alternative separately from participation and any non-consent consequences. Suppose ten verified NMA cost $20,000 and would receive a 20% royalty across a uniformly allocated 640-acre unit. A hypothetical $2,000,000 first-year sales base implies $6,250 before deductions; actual receipts depend on drilling, production timing, and decline. By contrast, a ten-sixty-fourths-percent calculation would be wrong: ten divided by 640 is 1.5625% working-interest participation, which allocates $156,250 of a hypothetical $10,000,000 well cost before other contractual or order-specific adjustments. That exposure dwarfs the purchase price. Do not transplant Oklahoma elections or cost-recovery rules into another state. Track purchaser substitution, service, effective ownership, and written election delivery with counsel. The fallback is explicit: stop acquisitions pending counsel review and choose only timely, fully understood permitted elections. If the seller cannot establish what has already been elected, suspend pricing rather than assuming a clean royalty conversion.

The remaining four plays need equally explicit unit math and fallbacks. Producing-royalty acquisition at $100,000 against $12,000 current annual receipts has a 12% initial gross cash yield; a 20% volume decline with unchanged realized pricing cuts the next year's receipts to $9,600. Reduce the offer or pass when the downside cannot support carrying costs. NPRI specialization can turn document expertise into better pricing, but a proposed $30,000 purchase supported by $4,000 annual receipts has only a 13.33% initial gross yield before expenses and decline; unresolved fraction language requires a pricing hold, not optimistic selection. Unleased-mineral lease-up might pair a $20,000 ten-NMA acquisition with a $5,000 bonus, but that bonus neither recovers the entire investment nor proves production. If no executable lease appears, retain only acreage affordable without near-term income. Institutional assembly might sell a package for $250,000 against $190,000 basis and $10,000 selling costs, leaving a $50,000 realized gain under this chapter's transaction convention. If the exit buyer withdraws, the fallback is a separately underwritten holding case, not a forced resale assumption. Never count one transaction simultaneously as an unrealized appraisal uplift, a full sale-price revenue event, and a realized trading gain.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Owner Revenue Without Counting the Same Capital Twice
paragraphs: The canonical revenue boundary is royalty receipts and realized rights-trading gains, excluding returned basis. It is an operator scorecard convention, not an assertion that every entity presents identical financial statements or tax returns. Maintain separate ledgers for production sales context, royalty settlement components, bank receipts, acquisition basis, selling costs, and realized gains. If a buyer pays $250,000 for interests with $190,000 carrying basis and $10,000 direct selling costs, the illustrative realized gain is $50,000; the $190,000 basis recovery is recycled capital, not new revenue. Record the $10,000 once in the gain calculation rather than deducting it again from scorecard profit. Unrealized valuation increases contribute zero to this realized-gain metric. Keep lease bonuses outside the canonical scenario bridge and identify their separate treatment in actual books. For royalties, preserve gross entitlement, tax withholding, deductions, and settlement adjustments even when the scorecard uses the settled receipt. Prior-period reversals belong in the reconciliation, not in a hidden exception folder. The entire unit's sales, an institutional buyer's assets under management, and the aggregate consideration circulating through a transaction chain are contextual amounts. None becomes this operator's revenue merely because their spreadsheet contains it.

Reconcile the three annual cases exactly before testing a more ambitious portfolio. Conservative generates $30,000 revenue, incurs $24,000 modeled expenses, and leaves $6,000 owner net profit at 20%. Base generates $215,000 revenue, incurs $145,125 modeled expenses, and leaves $69,875 at 32.5%. Scaled generates $400,000 revenue, incurs $220,000 modeled expenses, and leaves $180,000 at 45%. An illustrative composition is $24,000 royalties plus $6,000 realized gains for Conservative, $150,000 plus $65,000 for Base, and $280,000 plus $120,000 for Scaled. Those splits explain the arithmetic; they are not additional canonical forecasts. The supplied monthly operating range is $1,000–$12,000, while these margin-implied annual expenses can include costs outside recurring overhead. For example, modeled recurring overhead of $18,000, $96,000, and $144,000 leaves respective residual expense budgets of $6,000, $49,125, and $76,000 for separately identified activities. Actual classifications must come from the ledger, not from forcing invoices into a convenient residual. Acquisition principal remains investment capital rather than ordinary overhead. Preserve the canonical profit figures and team sizes while showing compensation, debt costs, transaction expenses, and owner distributions explicitly in any expanded operating model. Margin alone does not establish an investment return.

Capital productivity is the next underwriting question. A $69,875 Base owner profit supported by $1,000,000 of average invested equity implies a 6.9875% simple annual profit-to-equity ratio before any adjustments to that profit definition. The same profit supported by $250,000 implies 27.95%, but it requires evidence that acquisitions, holding periods, and exits actually permit that turnover. Neither ratio is supplied by the scorecard. Build monthly cash schedules because royalties arrive after production and sales, ownership transfers can enter suspense, and sale proceeds may include escrow holdbacks. Texas Natural Resources Code § 91.402 establishes payment timing rules with specified exceptions; do not equate a statutory entitlement with immediate bank availability. Stress commodity pricing and volumes independently: a 20% price reduction combined with a 15% volume reduction leaves 68% of the original revenue before changes in deductions. A $12,000 receipt stream therefore becomes $8,160 under that simplified stress. Review depletion under 26 U.S.C. §§ 611 and 613A with the tax preparer, keeping tax deductions separate from bank cash and reserve depletion. Finally, maintain liquidity for title disputes and delayed transfers without relying on an uncontracted portfolio sale to pay next month's operating bills.

sections.heading: 4. Build a Title-and-Payment Evidence System That Survives the Exit
paragraphs: The durable moat is a repeatable evidence system spanning acquisition, payment, and resale. Create a tract identifier that persists across deeds, leases, wells, unit orders, division orders, and buyer schedules. Store instrument references, recording dates, grantor and grantee names, depth restrictions, ownership fractions, and unresolved exceptions as structured fields with links to source images. Track document revisions rather than overwriting a fraction when a new interpretation arrives. A recorded mineral deed is central, but recording alone does not establish that the grantor owned everything purportedly conveyed. Counsel-directed title work must address the relevant chain, reservations, probate transfers, liens, and conveyance requirements. The land professional gathers and organizes evidence; counsel resolves legal interpretation; the principal owns the price decision. Give each exception a financial consequence: withheld purchase consideration, a tract exclusion, a specific cure, or a decision to pass. This turns title work into underwriting rather than a ceremonial report. At exit, a buyer should reproduce ownership and projected receipts from the package without relying on the seller's memory. The resulting reduction in diligence friction is more defensible than claims of access to secret acreage or universal discounts from distressed owners.

Automate royalty reconciliation and production monitoring only after establishing the correct ownership model. Import EnergyLink files or payer statements into a controlled ledger with production month, payment month, well identifier, product, volume, realized price, decimal, deductions, and net settlement. Match deposits to statements, then statements to the property schedule. Flag changed decimals, missing wells, negative adjustments, unusual deductions, and long gaps between reported production and receipts. Compare regulator production data on its reporting cadence; late filings and later revisions can explain apparent differences without proving underpayment. Use documented exception thresholds rather than alerting on every small rounding change. For example, a 0.003125 expected decimal appearing as 0.002500 deserves immediate investigation because it represents a 20% reduction in the calculated share. An alert should produce an evidence packet and owner-relations inquiry, not an automated accusation. Keep access permissions narrow, maintain backups, and preserve original files. In a dispute, reconstruct exactly which document and statement supported the payment expectation. Automation makes the principal more consistent and contractors more productive; it cannot determine a contested mineral fraction, compel drilling, or remove commodity exposure. Those remain judgment, contractual, and market risks that must be priced before committing capital.

Close with a pre-flight review that distinguishes an affordable investment from an attractive narrative. Confirm the seller's transferable interest, the payment formula, development assumptions, election status, funding source, and downside liquidity before releasing purchase funds. Independently verify changed wire instructions through a previously established contact channel. For pooled outside capital, analyze the actual instrument and offering structure before solicitation: 15 U.S.C. § 77b(a)(1) expressly includes fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its securities definition, and § 77e addresses registration-related prohibitions absent an applicable exemption. Do not infer an exemption from calling participants partners or describing ownership as passive acreage. Separately establish entity authority, tax reporting responsibility, property-tax calendars, and who may sign leases or elections. A disciplined small team wins by rejecting unbounded obligations while completing bounded transactions quickly. The startup capital range of $15,000–$75,000 must support both owned assets and a realistic cash reserve; it is not a target purchase price for the first tract. Advance only when the holding case works without an immediate institutional exit. The operating result is a portfolio whose ownership, cash receipts, and realized gains remain explainable under buyer diligence, payer corrections, and an unfavorable commodity cycle.

chapters.question_prompt: Who writes the check in mineral rights, what acute financial or statutory pain forces them to pay, and how do funds clear cleanly without circumvention or non-payment?
chapters.title: Who Pays, Why They Pay & How the Payment Rail Works
chapters.subtitle: NMA and NPRI Underwriting, Division-Order Pay Decks, Pooling Dockets, Escrow Authority, and Texas Natural Resources Code Chapter 91
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 81/100. Checks come from production purchasers, operators acting as disbursers, mineral buyers, and co-owners purchasing documented interests; their authority and obligations differ. This chapter maps five operating plays: fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing, producing-royalty acquisition, pooling-docket acquisition, institutional aggregation flips, and purchased-interest suspense recovery. Only the first carries a supplied play identifier; the other four are chapter-level operating mappings. Each connects a payment trigger to title evidence, credit screening, settlement instructions, and a fallback. Canonical annual owner profits are $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled. Revenue means royalty receipts plus realized rights-trading gains, excluding returned basis. Protect collection through verified authority and controlled document release, not speculative remedies or production headlines.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the Actual Payor, Their Pain, and Their Spending Authority
paragraphs: Separate the economic beneficiary, the check writer, and the person authorized to release money. For producing interests, a purchaser of production or an operator's revenue department may remit royalties under the lease, division-order arrangements, and applicable payment statutes. The landman who discusses acreage usually cannot change the pay deck or authorize a suspense release. For an institutional acquisition, an acquisitions director sponsors the trade, an investment committee sets the ceiling, title counsel defines acceptable defects, and treasury funds the closing. For a family buyout, the sibling negotiating price might lack authority over an estate or trust. Obtain the relevant fiduciary instruments, entity resolutions, and signatory evidence before treating enthusiasm as buying power. Acute pain is concrete: a family wants estate liquidity, an institution needs contiguous exposure that fits its mandate, or a production payor must resolve documented payment obligations. None of these facts makes an unleased operator buy your minerals. Ask who owns the budget, which conditions release it, when treasury processes payments, and who can reject title. Record those answers separately from the broker's narrative. A transaction advances only when price, legal authority, and payment capacity converge on the same identified counterparty.

The mandatory TRACK_1 play, fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing, starts with a documented fractional estate, not a threat. Suppose an eighty-acre tract carries a verified one-quarter mineral interest: the acquisition covers twenty net mineral acres, before examining burdens and the precise estate conveyed. A $12,000 purchase followed by an $18,000 voluntary co-owner buyout produces $6,000 of gross realized gain before transaction expenses; the returned $12,000 is not revenue. The buyer pays for consolidation, reduced administration, and resolved ownership friction, not because a demand letter creates an unconditional duty to purchase. Inspect probate filings, deeds, reservations, marital interests, liens, and any existing lease before quoting that acreage. Texas Property Code Chapter 23A may alter partition procedure where the property qualifies as heirs' property; counsel must determine its application to the particular mineral estate and dispute. Appraisal, co-owner buyout opportunities, and partition preferences can defeat a simplistic forced-sale thesis. Budget the carrying period and litigation exposure before acquisition rather than using either as negotiating theater. The fallback is a renegotiated voluntary exit or continued ownership within the approved capital limit. Never threaten an unavailable remedy, conceal other owners' rights, or underwrite a compulsory buyout as certain cash.

Producing-royalty acquisition, the second operating mapping, purchases an existing payment entitlement rather than a collection service. Illustratively, $1,000,000 of monthly well-level sales value multiplied by a verified 0.001 royalty decimal yields $1,000 before permitted adjustments. That decimal must come from the lease, ownership chain, unit allocation, and applicable burdens; it cannot be inferred from net mineral acres alone. At a constant run rate, the example contributes $12,000 of annual gross entitlement, but underwriting must also model decline, commodity prices, downtime, and cash deductions. A nonparticipating royalty interest, or NPRI, does not automatically carry leasing authority or a share of bonuses. Read the granting and reservation language, including whether the fraction is fixed or floating. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 sets payment timing for covered proceeds and recognizes specified grounds for withholding; Section 91.403 addresses interest. These provisions do not turn disputed title into immediately collectible money. Screen the payor's financial condition and establish ownership in its records before forecasting a first deposit. If transfer processing stalls, retain seller cooperation, document the missing requirement, and distinguish recoverable suspense from a valuation loss caused by declining production.

callout.title: Find the Payment Department Before Negotiating the Multiple
callout.body: Payment friction usually appears first in ownership records, authority documents, or statement detail.
items: Ask the seller for three consecutive royalty statements and the payor's ownership-transfer checklist; match owner numbers before submitting the deed.
For NPRIs, extract the complete reservation clause into the underwriting file and have title counsel resolve fixed-versus-floating language before assigning a decimal.

Price fractional heir interests using documented carrying costs and voluntary exit alternatives, rather than assuming a court will deliver a quick sale.

sections.heading: 2. Match Each Obligation to a Settlement Rail That Can Actually Clear
paragraphs: Treat the eight payment choices as different control structures, not interchangeable buttons. Wire and ACH are transfer mechanisms; escrow and milestone holds are custody arrangements; retainers describe advance compensation; statutory disbursement describes an underlying obligation; platform checkout supplies an interface; factoring monetizes an eligible receivable. A mineral purchase commonly combines a wire with escrow, while recurring royalties commonly arrive by ACH under statutory and contractual rules. Choose the combination after identifying the asset, title conditions, actual payor, and remedy for failed performance. Use an escrow provider authorized and operationally equipped for the transaction, and confirm whether it handles severed minerals rather than assuming ordinary residential procedures fit. Written instructions should identify deposited documents, permitted disbursements, recording sequence, defect treatment, and the exact event allowing release. Verify bank instructions through an independently obtained telephone number and a second reviewer; an email thread alone cannot authenticate a last-minute account change. Do not let a seller's document-delivery obligation depend on an unverified screenshot of a pending transfer. Confirm receipt with the receiving institution or escrow holder under its actual settlement procedures. Recording and funding must follow a sequence both parties have expressly accepted.

For the pooling-docket acquisition mapping, public regulatory proceedings create an information schedule, not guaranteed production. In Oklahoma, review Oklahoma Corporation Commission filings, hearing materials, orders, and the actual election provisions under 52 O.S. Section 87.1. A proposed order, final order, and completed well are distinct events with different valuation consequences. An illustrative $30,000 acquisition resold for $45,000 yields $15,000 of gross realized gain before expenses, not $45,000 of operator revenue. Condition the purchase on verified ownership, the treatment of existing elections, and a precise description of rights conveyed. If a seller retains a pooling payment or an election has already been made, reflect that allocation in the agreement and price. The later institutional buyer pays for validated exposure and reduced research uncertainty; the commission does not fund your speculative resale. When an order is continued, challenged, or economically unattractive, the fallback is to retain the interest within a modeled carrying budget, renegotiate before a binding closing, or abandon an uncommitted acquisition. Do not promise a buyer an election option that has expired or assume a mineral purchase renews its deadline. Attach the operative order and deadline analysis to settlement instructions where either affects value.

Recurring disbursements need a different control file from asset purchases. For covered Texas proceeds, Section 91.402 generally starts with payment no later than 120 days after the end of the month of first sale; subsequent timing generally differs between oil and gas, subject to statutory provisions and permissible arrangements. Track the actual facts rather than applying one universal clock to every state and interest. Ownership disputes, minimum-payment provisions, and other specified conditions can change the collection analysis. Request the reason for withholding in writing and preserve the required notice history before pursuing remedies. ACH simplifies recurring receipts but remains subject to applicable return and reversal rules; do not describe it as unconditional finality. A platform receipt likewise proves only what the provider's records actually establish. Factoring requires a separate review of receivable existence, assignability, recourse, notification, perfection, and effective cost. If a factor advances $9,500 against a $10,000 eligible receivable and retains $500 as its fee, the fee consumes five percent of face value for that financing period, not five percent annually. Compare that cost against waiting, credit exposure, and contractual restrictions before assigning a royalty stream to solve a temporary cash shortage.

sections.heading: 3. Protect the Gain, Screen the Buyer, and Reconcile the Scorecard
paragraphs: Institutional aggregation flips, the fourth mapping, monetize a clean package rather than the gross dollars crossing escrow. For an illustrative Base bridge, purchase a package for $185,000 and sell it for $250,000: returned basis is $185,000 and gross realized gain is $65,000 before selling expenses. Combined with $150,000 of royalty receipts, recognized scorecard revenue is $215,000. Apply total modeled operating and transaction costs of $145,125 to reach the canonical $69,875 owner profit and 32.5% margin. The institution pays because verified acreage, burdens, ownership, and transfer files reduce its acquisition workload and fit its portfolio criteria. It does not pay extra merely because you compiled a large spreadsheet. Package pricing must expose parcel-level adjustments so a defect cannot silently destroy the margin on acceptable assets. Obtain a signed purchase commitment before incurring buyer-specific diligence that cannot be reused. If investment approval disappears, use staged acquisitions, alternative qualified buyers, or retention economics already supported by the royalty case. Do not buy an entire package with short-duration funding solely because an acquisitions employee expressed interest. The downside belongs in the capital plan before deeds are delivered, not in an optimistic resale narrative.

Keep all three annual scenarios tied to the supplied scorecard while treating internal receipt mixes as illustrations. Conservative revenue of $30,000 can comprise $24,000 of royalty receipts and $6,000 of realized trading gain; $24,000 of costs leaves $6,000 owner profit at 20%. Base remains $215,000 revenue, $145,125 costs, and $69,875 profit at 32.5%. Scaled revenue of $400,000 can comprise $280,000 of royalty receipts and $120,000 of realized gains; $220,000 of costs leaves $180,000 profit at 45%. Conservative and Base each use 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C, six people. These are annual operating cases, not acquisition capital recovery schedules or guaranteed staffing productivity. The supplied startup capital range is $15,000 to $75,000, monthly operating expense range is $1,000 to $12,000, and time to first deal is six to twenty-four months. Annual scenario costs are broader than a monthly overhead budget and must be reconciled through actual categories rather than forced into that range. Track purchase basis, transaction expenses, royalty deductions, financing charges, and owner distributions separately. A large closing wire can improve liquidity while adding only a modest amount to recognized revenue.

Fee protection begins by naming what is actually earned. An owner selling minerals earns a trading gain; an intermediary earns a separately contracted fee subject to applicable licensing and transaction rules. Do not invoice your own principal profit as a commission or assume a confidentiality agreement creates payment rights. Where lawful services are separately engaged, identify the fee obligor, specific introduced assets or counterparties, earning event, payment deadline, permitted tail, and dispute process. If payment is to come through closing, obtain written agreement from the responsible parties and escrow holder. A buyer's acknowledgment of an introduction is weaker than an executed payment obligation. Screen institutional counterparties using entity records, signatory authority, available financial statements, litigation and insolvency searches, and financing conditions; SEC EDGAR helps when the relevant entity reports publicly. Verify current funding evidence directly through an authorized channel rather than trusting a forwarded bank image. Review applicable lien records where receivables or assets secure credit. A special-purpose buyer with no assets requires funded consideration or negotiated credit support, not confidence borrowed from its sponsor's logo. Narrow noncircumvention terms to legitimate documented services; payment evidence and closing control provide stronger protection than expansive threats against everyone who sees the offering.

sections.heading: 4. Run the Receipt-to-Reconciliation Workflow and Escalate Real Exceptions
paragraphs: Purchased-interest suspense recovery, the fifth mapping, realizes rights that were acquired with documented entitlement to withheld proceeds. Buying minerals does not automatically transfer every historical receivable, so the agreement must allocate pre-effective-date and post-effective-date proceeds, adjustment rights, and seller cooperation. Illustratively, eight months of properly attributable $1,000 monthly payments creates an $8,000 gross suspense claim, not an $8,000 recovery fee. That amount can form part of the royalty-receipt bucket once collected; never add it again as trading gain. Verify whether the balance reflects title suspense, a minimum-payment threshold, returned mail, bank rejection, or an actual ownership dispute. Those categories demand different documents and produce different collection times. Ask the payor for its written requirements, submit a complete indexed package, and record acknowledgment. The fallback is a discounted carrying value, a contractual seller cure, or an appropriately supported claim through counsel, depending on the defect. Do not assume statutory interest applies to every withheld balance or that a new deed resolves an older probate gap. If the proceeds were remitted as unclaimed property, follow the responsible state's claim process rather than demanding that the payor send the same funds twice.

Build a receipt ledger that joins legal ownership to production months and bank deposits. Store the tract identifier, well identifier, payor owner number, interest type, effective date, decimal, product, volume, price, deductions, adjustments, and payment reference. Use EnergyLink statements where available, payor portals, and retained source documents; a spreadsheet can work initially if changes remain reviewable and source files are preserved. Railroad Commission of Texas production records and Oklahoma Corporation Commission records support monitoring, but public reports may use reporting units and timing that differ from revenue statements. Reconcile those differences before accusing a payor of underpayment. Automation should flag missing periods, changed decimals, unusual deductions, and deposits lacking statements; it should not automatically declare every variance collectible. Match a $1,000 expected gross entitlement to the actual statement's deductions and adjustments before comparing the net deposit. Document whether each adjustment is supported by lease language and applicable law. Separate an accounting correction from a commodity-price decline or depletion signal. This is where royalty reconciliation and production monitoring reduce labor without replacing title judgment. Assign one person to own each exception and require a dated next action so an unattended suspense item cannot masquerade as a healthy receivable.

Escalation should follow evidence and the controlling agreement rather than emotional pressure. Start with the relevant revenue or closing department, submit the exact exception with supporting records, and request a dated written response. Next, use the contractual notice process and any applicable statutory prerequisites. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.404 includes notice and response procedures relevant to an action for covered unpaid proceeds and interest; counsel should map those requirements to the particular claim. Preserve versions of division orders, transfer requests, correspondence, statements, and settlement instructions. Keep seller cooperation duties alive long enough to complete ownership transfers and address agreed historical adjustments. If capital comes from multiple investors, review the actual offering structure before solicitation: 15 U.S.C. Section 77b(a)(1) expressly includes fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its securities definition. Registration, exemptions, disclosure, and intermediary rules depend on the arrangement and activity; a direct-asset label does not settle the analysis. Close each month with three separate views: royalty cash collected, trading gains realized, and capital still invested. That discipline makes buyer credit deterioration, depleted production, and unresolved title visible before a headline account balance persuades the team to fund another acquisition.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 81/100: attractive asset margins, demanding capital deployment, and stubborn title labor. This chapter maps five operating plays: producing-mineral acquisition, NPRI aggregation, pooling-docket curve-jumping, institutional rights flips, and cell_tower_billboard_easement_strip_out. Only royalty receipts and realized rights-trading gains enter the canonical revenue cases; returned purchase basis never becomes revenue. Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner profits reconcile to $6,000, $69,875, and $180,000 on $30,000, $215,000, and $400,000 revenue. The operating model separates payor deductions, acquisition capital, contractor expense, realized corrections, and liquidity reserves. It then sizes payout-lock runway without double-counting receivables and tests commodity declines, depletion, title defects, and delayed institutional closings.

sections.heading: 1. Price the conveyed decimal before pricing the opportunity
paragraphs: Start the cohort ledger with the property interest, not the seller's headline acreage. Net mineral acres, or NMA, equal gross tract acres multiplied by the mineral ownership fraction; they do not establish the royalty decimal without lease and allocation terms. For a simple 640-acre pooled unit containing 20 NMA under a one-fifth royalty, the illustrative decimal is 20 / 640 × 0.20 = 0.00625. At $200,000 of monthly unit proceeds before owner-specific deductions, that decimal produces $1,250 of gross entitlement. A $100 supported deduction leaves $1,150 of receipts, or $13,800 annualized before decline and operator expenses. A $92,000 purchase therefore shows a 15% current cash yield, not a 15% permanent return. Verify tract participation, allocation-well treatment, effective dates, and product-specific decimals before using this shortcut. An NPRI may be a fixed fraction of production or a floating fraction of royalty; mechanically multiplying every instrument by the lease royalty can materially misprice the interest. Build separate oil, gas, and natural-gas-liquids schedules, attach the conveyance and lease language, and make the title reviewer sign off on the arithmetic rather than merely the county recording references.

Map five plays into this same ledger without pretending they share identical legal rights. Producing-mineral acquisition buys the $13,800 receipt stream above; its fallback is a smaller purchase supported by existing production rather than speculative locations. NPRI aggregation might combine ten independently verified interests costing $8,000 each into an $80,000 basis package. A $100,000 sale generates $20,000 of gross trading gain, not $100,000 of revenue; $5,000 of selling and delivery expense leaves $15,000 contribution. Pooling-docket curve-jumping might place $40,000 at risk ahead of a public hearing and target a $55,000 sale, producing $15,000 before expenses. Its fallback is a producing-value bid or withdrawal, because an application is neither an order nor a producing well. Institutional rights flips require buyer-ready title and an independently supportable basis rollforward; the Base illustration sells $245,000 of basis for $310,000 and recognizes $65,000 of gross gain. If the buyer reprices, retain the income-producing interests only when their standalone cash yield supports the carrying cost. These examples explain underwriting mechanics; they are not additive transactions secretly layered onto the canonical annual cases.

The fifth play, cell_tower_billboard_easement_strip_out, is an adjacent rights-separation strategy, not a mineral royalty subtype. Separate assignable site-access and rent rights from underlying real estate only after examining the actual lease, easement, mortgage, and transfer provisions. Suppose $18,000 of annual rent supports a specialist buyer's $180,000 offer. If the allocated basis of the conveyed interest is $120,000 and closing costs are $10,000, the gross realized gain is $60,000 and the contribution is $50,000. Returned basis remains $120,000. If the permanent access burden reduces the retained property's value by $25,000, the economic improvement is only $25,000, even though that residual impairment may have different accounting treatment. A tenant cancellation clause can destroy the presumed duration premium; model termination at the first exercisable date instead of capitalizing rent indefinitely. The fallback is to retain the lease or negotiate a narrower term-limited assignment with all required approvals. Keep this adjacent illustration outside the mineral scorecard totals. Across all five plays, the reusable discipline is identical: specify the asset sold, identify the cash-flow owner, allocate basis defensibly, and charge the transaction for burdens left behind.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile every cohort dollar from receipts to owner profit
paragraphs: The following waterfall is an illustrative expense allocation constrained to the canonical scorecard, not a claim that the scorecard supplied these individual cost buckets. Conservative revenue comprises $24,000 of royalty receipts and $6,000 of realized rights-trading gains; Base comprises $150,000 and $65,000; Scaled comprises $280,000 and $120,000. These sums equal $30,000, $215,000, and $400,000. Royalty receipts here mean amounts credited after payor-level deductions, before the buyer's operating expenses. Reconcile gross entitlement to those receipts in a supporting schedule, but never subtract the same transportation or production-tax withholding again in the owner waterfall. Trading gains are sale proceeds less allocated acquisition basis, before separately budgeted selling costs. Capitalized acquisition costs belong in basis; recurring origination and failed-deal acquisition spending belong in the expense model. The table then deducts $24,000, $145,125, and $220,000 respectively, delivering exactly $6,000, $69,875, and $180,000 of annual owner profit. Divide those profits by recognized revenue to obtain 20%, 32.5%, and 45%. For this management illustration, owner profit is the residual before personal income taxes, with no separate deduction for the owner's unpaid labor or distributions.

Contractor delivery labor is $6,000, $36,000, and $54,000 across the three cases. A Base operating budget can purchase 180 landman hours at $100, 60 title-counsel hours at $200, and 120 reconciliation hours at $50, totaling $36,000. Those hours describe recurring diligence, exception resolution, and reconciliation expense; any work properly capitalized to a purchased asset moves into basis and requires an offsetting budget reconciliation. Acquisition CAC is separately $3,000, $24,000, and $36,000. At Base, twelve closed seller relationships imply $2,000 of origination cost per relationship, including failed outreach and unsuccessful negotiations but excluding the acquisition price. Do not report CAC per deed when one seller signs several instruments. The scorecard teams are 1 FT plus 3 contractors, 1 FT plus 3 contractors, and 2 FT plus 4 contractors. Contractor counts represent available specialists rather than full-time equivalent payroll. The Conservative case is an owner-operated asset platform, not a business paying a market salary from $6,000 of profit. Scaled requires explicit allocation of the second full-time role within the $36,000 overhead budget or a disclosed owner participation arrangement; silently adding payroll breaks the published profit.

Data and administration cover Enverus or other production-data subscriptions, county copies, accounting support, and storage, subject to actual vendor quotes rather than assumed enterprise access. Asset charges cover costs not already withheld by payors, such as applicable property taxes, carrying charges, and separately expensed disposition costs. Financing is $3,000, $18,000, and $30,000; the Base amount can represent a $150,000 average drawn balance at 12% annual interest. Principal repayment is a financing cash movement, never an operating expense. Realized scrub and reversal losses are $1,500, $8,000, and $10,000, capturing validated ownership corrections, collection shortfalls, and unrecovered overpayments. Do not also reduce royalty receipts for those same losses. A liquidity reserve is different: transferring $10,000 into restricted internal cash does not create another expense. Track reserve usage against actual losses and replenish from available cash. Tax depletion under 26 U.S.C. sections 611 and 613A requires a separate tax schedule; it is neither a substitute for geological decline nor automatic cash available for distributions. This management waterfall does not purport to calculate tax-basis income or financial-statement depletion. Preserve those bridges so accounting presentation cannot conceal deteriorating asset economics.

sections.heading: 3. Finance the payout lock without counting the same gap twice
paragraphs: Treat mineral cash conversion as two clocks: production-to-payment and purchase-to-transfer acceptance. A seller can convey a valid interest while the payor still needs recorded documents, tax identification, ownership setup, and a corrected division order. Model days sales outstanding as the interval from production-month entitlement to cleared funds, then separately record any incremental transfer hold. Do not stack a 90-day DSO assumption and a 90-day suspense assumption if they describe the same withheld months. At Base, $150,000 of annual receipts implies $12,500 monthly. A 90-day lock using a twelve-month convention exposes $37,500 of expected receipts to timing risk. That number measures delayed collections, not an additional expense or certain bad debt. A rolling thirteen-week cash forecast should show opening cash, actual payment dates, purchase settlements, contractor invoices, interest, and minimum reserves. Mark disputed receivables separately from ordinary payment lag. Texas Natural Resources Code section 91.402 provides payment timing rules and conditions for withholding; it does not make every 90-day forecast delay permissible. Record the reason for each hold and obtain a dated payor response before counting the release as available liquidity.

Size opening runway from actual outflows rather than adding every alarming balance. Base annual expenses of $145,125 average $12,093.75 monthly, including $1,500 of interest. Excluding interest, the $10,593.75 monthly average fits within the stated $1,000–$12,000 operating-expense range; annual averages still conceal lumpy closing costs. Three months of total modeled outflows require $36,281.25. Add a separately designated $10,000 liquidity reserve and the opening operating buffer becomes $46,281.25. This assumes no collections during those months and smooth expense timing; replace it with invoice-level peaks before funding. Do not add the $37,500 delayed-receipt balance again: the zero-collection runway already funds those months' outflows. If the alternative model starts from a fully funded steady-state balance sheet, calculate the incremental collection delay instead, but use one funding method consistently. For an illustrative $400,000 asset deployment, total opening uses are $446,281.25. A $150,000 facility allocated to purchases leaves $296,281.25 of equity funding. This fits the stated $15,000–$75,000 startup range without implying every portfolio can borrow at the assumed rate or close within the 6–24 month first-deal window.

Institutional exits create a second liquidity trap because purchase basis can look like spendable operating cash. In the Base illustration, a $310,000 closing receipt contains $245,000 of returned basis and only $65,000 of gross trading gain. Route closing proceeds through a settlement bridge showing basis recovery, transaction expenses, required debt repayment, holdbacks, and genuinely distributable cash. Returned basis may fund replacement assets, but doing so consumes cash that cannot simultaneously cover distributions. A contractual $20,000 escrow holdback changes collection timing even when a gain is otherwise recognized; analyze recognition and collectability separately with the accountant. If closing itself moves beyond year-end, the illustrative Base gain disappears from that year's realized revenue. Preserve a pre-exit and post-exit cash forecast rather than treating a buyer's letter of intent as financing. Borrowing documents may restrict assignments, require proceeds sweeps, or exclude disputed royalties from collateral availability. Inspect those provisions before promising the next purchase. An additional month without any collections requires $12,093.75 more Base runway under this model, while another $12,500 of expected royalties is delayed; those are two descriptions of exposure, not automatically two additive funding requirements.

sections.heading: 4. Stress price, depletion, title corrections, and exit timing separately
paragraphs: Run sensitivity tests against receipts, not against the entire asset purchase price or merchant-style transaction volume. The simplest commodity test cuts royalty receipts 20% while holding trading gains and operating expenses constant. Conservative profit falls from $6,000 to $1,200; Base falls from $69,875 to $39,875; Scaled falls from $180,000 to $124,000. This is a deliberately transparent first-order test, not a prediction that realized prices, deductions, and taxes move uniformly. Add a separate 15% production decline and the combined royalty multiplier is 0.80 × 0.85 = 0.68, not 0.65. The resulting profits are a $1,680 loss, $21,875, and $90,400. Actual decline curves should distinguish new flush production from mature wells, planned downtime, workovers, and temporary curtailment. Pull monthly volumes from the Railroad Commission of Texas or the relevant state agency, then reconcile reporting scope and lag against payor statements. A lease-level gas series cannot automatically validate an individual well's allocation. Revise bids when the stress case consumes the reserve; increasing assumed future drilling merely hides the weakness of the existing producing base.

Labor and acquisition efficiency deserve their own tests because neither improves automatically with higher commodity prices. A 25% increase in contractor delivery expense reduces owner profit by $1,500, $9,000, and $13,500 across the cases. A 25% CAC overrun reduces it by $750, $6,000, and $9,000. Track title hours per accepted interest, rejected seller packages per closing, and reconciliation exceptions per payor rather than celebrating raw leads. An additional scrub loss equal to 5% of modeled royalty receipts costs $1,200, $7,500, and $14,000; it is incremental to the waterfall's existing realized-loss budget. Hold the opening cash reserve apart from that earnings calculation and test whether it still covers near-term payments after the loss. A three-percentage-point rate increase on Base's $150,000 average debt balance adds $4,500 of annual interest, reducing profit to $65,375. If credit availability also shrinks, recalculate equity needs instead of assuming the same facility remains usable. Automation belongs in statement ingestion, decimal matching, and production alerts; interpretation of an NPRI reservation or a contested succession chain remains a specialist decision with a recorded evidence trail.

Exit timing is the harshest test for a platform whose annual gain depends on one buyer. Remove that year's realized trading gains while retaining all modeled expenses: Conservative reaches zero profit, Base falls to $4,875, and Scaled falls to $60,000. These figures assume the assets remain owned and no additional impairment or carrying expense arises; extend the cash forecast if either assumption fails. Before funding, verify severed mineral title, lease burdens, payor transfer requirements, and the buyer's acceptance criteria. Texas payment rules and division-order requirements must be applied to the actual facts, including permissible withholding conditions and contractual payment provisions. Pooling and spacing orders require jurisdiction-specific review; a map overlay is not an ownership opinion. If outside investors fund fractional interests or a managed vehicle, analyze securities status under 15 U.S.C. section 77b and registration or exemption requirements before solicitation. Fractional undivided mineral interests appear expressly in the statutory definition of a security. Finish each investment memorandum with a downside purchase price, a funded holding period, and an executable fallback. Institutional-quality economics begin when the operator can decline an attractive-looking deal without endangering existing obligations.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you allocate startup capital ($15,000–$75,000 USD) and configure a lean, low-opex ($1,000–$12,000 USD/mo) production stack without wasting cash on bloated overhead?

chapters.subtitle: Reserve-First NMA and NPRI Underwriting, County Title Evidence, Royalty Reconciliation, and FERC Queue-Signal Discipline
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 81/100: capital discipline matters more than subscription count. This chapter maps five operating plays: producing-mineral purchases, NPRI purchases, pooling-docket curve-jumping, institutional rights flips, and FERC queue-informed land options. Keep at least half of startup capital untouched as liquidity, buy evidence before acreage, and separate mineral ownership from surface access and electricity service. A twelve-layer stack supports title packets, production monitoring, and royalty reconciliation without enterprise overhead. Canonical annual owner profits remain $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled. The operating test is executable title, traceable receipts, controlled downside, and enough cash to survive the full 6–24-month first-deal window.

sections.heading: 1. Ring-fence liquidity before pricing the first mineral deed
paragraphs: Start with a capital ledger, not an acreage target. At $150,000, place $90,000 in a separately tracked working-capital reserve, allocate $30,000 to rights purchases, $7,500 to title and technical diligence, $5,000 to contingent options, $4,000 to entity and insurance setup, $3,500 to data and systems, and $10,000 to transaction contingencies. These amounts total $150,000; the reserve is 60% of opening capital. At $2,000,000, allocate $1,100,000 to reserve, $650,000 to rights, $80,000 to diligence, $40,000 to options, $30,000 to setup, $20,000 to systems, and $80,000 to contingencies. That reserve is 55%. Neither reserve is acquisition capacity, collateral for an option, or a second name for committed purchase money. Release acquisition funds only after recording all outstanding exercises, title invoices, and closing costs. At the stated overhead endpoints, twenty-four months consumes $24,000 or $288,000, leaving $66,000 or $812,000 of the original reserve before receipts. Those runway calculations exclude deal-specific expenses, which belong in their own allocations. If overhead rises, reduce the acquisition envelope before signing another commitment. The 6–24-month first-deal window makes liquidity an operating input, not idle money awaiting a persuasive seller.

Reconcile the scorecard before evaluating any software proposal. Conservative revenue of $30,000 less $24,000 of total expenses produces $6,000 of owner profit, exactly 20%. Base revenue of $215,000 less $145,125 produces $69,875, exactly 32.5%. Scaled revenue of $400,000 less $220,000 produces $180,000, exactly 45%. One illustrative expense bridge assigns monthly fixed overhead of $1,000, $4,000, and $12,000 respectively; annual fixed costs are $12,000, $48,000, and $144,000, leaving $12,000, $97,125, and $76,000 for all remaining recognized expenses. These are allocation constraints, not estimates of what every county or contractor will charge. Do not add acquisition principal to operating expense and then also deduct it from trading proceeds. Track asset basis, capitalized acquisition costs, depletion, disposition proceeds, and recurring expenses separately under the adopted accounting method. The teams remain 1 FT plus 3 contractors in Conservative and Base, and 2 FT plus 4 contractors in Scaled. Contractor counts describe scoped specialists, not four continuous salaries. Treat the owner as one full-time operator; any additional salary or benefit expense must fit the existing expense envelope. Personal income taxes and owner distributions require separate cash planning.

Build the ownership and payment structure before circulating offers. Use the entity's exact legal name consistently on purchase agreements, deeds, tax forms, bank instructions, and operator ownership-transfer packets. A state-filed limited liability company can simplify administration, but it does not repair a broken mineral chain or change an NPRI into executive rights. Obtain an EIN, adopt signing authority, maintain a distinct ledger, and reconcile the operating account monthly. Mercury's Standard account can serve as a low-fee interface; examine the actual partner-bank and sweep arrangements rather than treating the interface as the insured bank. Aggregate deposits by ownership category and underlying bank when reviewing FDIC coverage. Bind coverage for actual activities: general liability for field visits, cyber and social-engineering exposures where available, and professional coverage only where the business performs services that require it. Ask specifically whether mineral title, contract disputes, pollution, and wire fraud are excluded. Do not assume a surface title policy insures severed minerals. Obtain closing instructions through an independently verified telephone number, use transaction counsel or an appropriate escrow provider, and prohibit emailed bank-detail changes from becoming payment authority without a callback.

callout.body: A commitment must pass all four tests using dated evidence and a named reviewer.

sections.heading: 2. Assemble twelve inexpensive layers around an auditable tract ledger
paragraphs: Make the tract ledger the system of record. Each asset needs a stable identifier, state and county, legal description, gross acres, acquired fraction, net mineral acres, interest type, lease references, unit allocation, operator, well identifiers, payment decimal, acquisition basis, and document links. Keep NMA distinct from royalty-adjusted acreage; a marketing convention using an eighth royalty must never overwrite the actual deed fraction. Store the original instrument alongside a structured extraction and a reviewer decision. Python and SQLite are sufficient for a small portfolio when backups, validation, and access restrictions are real. Use decimal arithmetic for money and ownership fractions, retain source precision, and round only at a documented reporting boundary. QGIS connects tract polygons to units, wells, surface constraints, and substations without an enterprise mapping contract. A spatial intersection is a research lead, not a title conclusion. County index gaps, duplicate names, ambiguous aliquot descriptions, and stale unit polygons require human resolution. Keep ownership assertions separate from machine-derived geometry so an attractive map cannot silently become an approved purchase premise. Export the ledger and its document manifest monthly so switching vendors never requires rebuilding the title record.

Use the twelve-layer matrix as a procurement baseline rather than a claim of live vendor quotations. The paid prices are explicit planning assumptions for named tiers, excluding taxes, promotions, optional services, and future changes; confirm vendor checkout terms before purchase. One Google Workspace Business Starter seat at $7 per month on an annual commitment and one DocuSign Personal subscription at $10 monthly equivalent imply $204 in annual subscription commitments. At the listed S3 Standard storage rate, twenty gigabytes adds $0.46 monthly before requests, transfer, or version accumulation. That makes the basic subscription-and-storage subtotal $17.46 per month, not the whole operating budget. County copies, counsel, landmen, insurance, bookkeeping labor, and technical review still consume the $1,000–$12,000 monthly envelope or separately budgeted deal costs. Avoid buying commercial production datasets until public records demonstrably fail a defined task. Test ten representative wells and three complete ownership files before upgrading. Measure missing months, mismatched identifiers, and reviewer hours, then compare the measured correction cost with an actual subscription proposal. A cheap dataset that creates expensive false positives is not a lean purchase.

Automate ingestion and exception detection, not ownership judgments. Download permitted public production files on a documented cadence, save retrieval dates and source hashes, and preserve the original royalty statement before normalizing its rows. Reconcile operator checks by production month, product, property, decimal, price, taxes, deductions, and suspense adjustments. Compare reported volumes with public records only after accounting for reporting delays, unit aggregation, gas measurement conventions, and corrections. Flag a decimal change immediately; flag a missing check against contractual timing and the jurisdiction's payment rules rather than an arbitrary calendar date. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 supplies specific payment timing and withholding provisions for covered proceeds. A dashboard should show the disputed amount, evidence, owner, and next action instead of merely coloring a cell red. Restrict bank access to the operator and authorized backup, require multifactor authentication, and keep tax identifiers out of source repositories. Encrypt offline backups, restrict document storage, and test restoration quarterly. Have the contract landman inspect title exceptions, the petroleum specialist inspect production assumptions, and the accountant inspect cash-to-ledger differences. One accountable owner closes each exception before the next acquisition relies on the same data.

callout.title: Four habits that save more than another data subscription
callout.body: Spend on resolving ownership and payment uncertainty before paying for prettier coverage.
items: Save the recorded image and recording reference, not just the county index result; reservations and exceptions often sit inside the instrument.
Preserve every royalty statement revision and its production month so recoupments do not masquerade as fresh production deterioration.
Store fixed and floating NPRI interpretations as separate underwriting cases until counsel resolves the deed language; never average incompatible ownership meanings.
Require a dated queue document and independent surface-access evidence before paying for a land option; a nearby substation is not a service commitment.

sections.heading: 3. Budget five operating plays without manufacturing revenue or secured power
paragraphs: The first two mapped plays are producing-mineral purchases and NPRI purchases; these are descriptive workflows, not additional scorecard scenarios. For producing minerals, assume ten NMA uniformly participate in a 640-acre unit under a 20% lease royalty, with no allocation adjustments. The modeled revenue decimal is 10 divided by 640 times 0.20, or 0.003125. Applied to $80,000 of monthly unit sales value, that produces $250 before owner-level deductions and taxes. A $30,000 purchase therefore shows $3,000 annualized receipts and a 10% initial cash yield, not a 10% profit margin or a perpetual annuity. Stress price, volumes, deductions, and depletion separately. For an NPRI burdening an 80-acre tract within that same unit, a fixed 1/64 fraction of production produces $156.25 monthly, while a floating one-quarter of a 20% lease royalty produces $500. Those calculations assume uniform tract participation and expose why deed interpretation dominates spreadsheet precision. An $8,000 offer cannot rely on the larger result until title review supports it. If production economics fail, lower the price or pass; if NPRI meaning remains disputed, require curative evidence or withdraw rather than pricing ambiguity as assured upside.

The third play, pooling-docket curve-jumping, buys or options an interest because a public proceeding may improve buyer attention, not because a hearing guarantees drilling. Read the actual application, spacing description, requested relief, notice record, and subsequent orders. An illustrative transaction spends $2,000 on an option, $3,000 on eligible acquisition diligence, and $25,000 on exercise, producing $30,000 of assumed basis. A $40,000 sale with $2,000 of selling costs yields $8,000 of realized gain and returns $30,000 of basis; the $40,000 proceeds are not all operator revenue. If the proceeding slips or the title cannot close, let the option expire and cap the sunk exposure at the amounts actually committed. The fourth play, institutional rights flipping, needs a buyer-quality package before acquisition: indexed instruments, tract schedules, lease terms, payment history, and a reproducible ownership decimal. Purchasing rights for $100,000, adding $10,000 of eligible basis costs, and selling for $145,000 with $5,000 selling costs creates $30,000 of realized gain and returns $110,000 of basis. If the buyer disappears, retain only assets whose stressed royalty economics independently justify the purchase. Otherwise reduce exposure before closing, rather than treating an indicative bid as cash.

The fifth mapped play is ferc_grid_interconnection_queue_land_speculation, the TRACK_1 FERC / ISO Substation Interconnection Queue & Powered-Land Option Flipping workflow. Overlay the correct ISO or utility queue with substations, parcels, zoning, floodplain, access, and transmission constraints. Distinguish generator interconnection from the load-service process relevant to an industrial user. Queue position, study progress, and nearby infrastructure are signals; none conveys deliverable power, surface control, easements, or transferable interconnection rights. Assume a $5,000 assignable option on 45 acres with a $225,000 exercise price, plus $4,000 of studies. A permitted $15,000 option assignment produces an illustrative $6,000 gain if the $9,000 expenditure is properly included in basis and there are no further selling costs. The $225,000 exercise obligation remains outside that assignment calculation and must never be silently funded from protected reserves. Counsel must confirm assignability and the accounting treatment. Under 18 CFR 35.28, applicable tariffs and interconnection procedures govern relevant service processes; a land marketer cannot replace them with promotional language. If access, service feasibility, or assignment fails, let the contingent option lapse with $9,000 exposure, or reposition only for independently viable uses without claiming secured power.

sections.heading: 4. Rehearse closing, collection, and failure before launching acquisition outreach
paragraphs: Run a dry closing on one representative tract before scaling outreach. Start with the seller's claimed interest and trace every required conveyance, reservation, probate event, and entity succession through the chosen title standard. Texas Property Code Section 5.021 addresses written conveyances of covered estates; Section 13.001 addresses the effect of recording against specified subsequent parties. Neither a recorded deed nor a county search result independently proves that the seller owns the fraction advertised. Ask transaction counsel to identify exceptions, required curative instruments, acknowledgment requirements, and county recording practices. Compare the resulting ownership fraction with the lease, unit documents, division order, and most recent check detail. Confirm that any executive rights, bonus rights, delay rentals, and development rights are actually included rather than assumed from the word minerals. Assemble a closing packet containing the purchase agreement, deed, recording instructions, settlement statement, identity and authority evidence, tax documentation, and operator notification materials. Rehearse the failed-close branch as carefully as the successful branch: return unused escrow under the contract, terminate outstanding permissions, calendar option expiry, and preserve the reasons for rejection so the same defective interest does not reenter the pipeline under another seller.

Then rehearse the first ninety days after funding without assuming the first check arrives immediately. Record the instrument, retain the recording confirmation, submit the operator's transfer package, and track requests for additional documentation. Division-order processing can delay payments, while disputed ownership can create suspense balances that remain unavailable for overhead. Establish a property-level receivable log showing production periods, expected decimal, paid amounts, deductions, and unresolved differences. Use the applicable lease and state payment rules when escalating a missing payment. For Texas assets, evaluate the circumstances against Section 91.402 rather than promising one universal check date. Have the accountant maintain acquisition basis and depletion schedules under the applicable tax rules, including 26 U.S.C. 611 and 612, instead of applying an automatic deduction percentage to every receipt. Track state severance withholding, property assessments where applicable, and filing obligations by jurisdiction. Do not net an operator's entire sales statement into business revenue when most production belongs to other interests. Post only the owned interest's royalty receipts and realized rights gains on the scorecard basis. A reconciliation is complete only when the bank deposit, statement detail, and ledger entry agree or a documented exception has an accountable owner.

Finally, establish a release decision that can survive an absent founder and a bad market. Give each specialist a written scope: the landman assembles evidence, counsel resolves legal ownership questions, the technical reviewer tests decline and allocation assumptions, and the accountant verifies treatment and reconciliation. At smaller scale, these are scoped contractor assignments rather than permanent departments. Fund the actual scopes inside the canonical expense limits before representing the team as operational. Require a second-person check of outgoing wire instructions and ownership decimals; retain the review record with the deal. Test whether the portfolio survives six months without a new sale, a 30% commodity-price reduction, and a production decline that the technical reviewer considers plausible for the assets. These are sensitivity tests, not replacements for the three canonical profit cases. If raising pooled capital, resolve the offering structure before soliciting investors: 15 U.S.C. 77b includes specified fractional mineral interests in its securities definition, and Section 77e governs registration requirements subject to applicable exemptions. Keep subscriber money distinct from operator revenue. Launch only after restoring a backup, reconciling a sample check, completing the title packet, and demonstrating that every outstanding commitment fits outside the protected opening reserve.

chapters.pull_quote: Buy evidence before acreage, protect liquidity before upside, and never sell a queue signal as secured power.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: capital discipline matters more than acquisition volume. This chapter maps five operator plays: NMA/NPRI title underwriting, pooling-docket curve-jumping, institutional flips, royalty reconciliation, and tcpa_litigator_scrub_honeypot_arbitrage. Each receives explicit unit math, failure signals, and a fallback that preserves capital or stops unauthorized outreach. Canonical annual owner profits are $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled; returned acquisition basis never becomes revenue. The question's 80% is a stress-test framing, not an established failure statistic. The practical enemies are defective conveyances, optimistic production curves, recoupable checks, adverse lease deductions, deceptive seller contact, and funding structures that turn a small title mistake into an uncapped obligation.
