sections.heading: 1. Underwrite the Conveyed Interest Before Pricing the Production
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is buying a spreadsheet description instead of the interest actually conveyed. In the NMA/NPRI title underwriting play, ten net mineral acres in a 640-acre unit at a 20% lease royalty produce an illustrative decimal of 10 / 640 x 0.20 = 0.003125. Against $100,000 of royalty-bearing proceeds before applicable adjustments, that decimal implies $312.50, not $2,000. This shortcut works only when the unit allocation, mineral ownership, and lease terms support it. A nonparticipating royalty interest may instead be fixed or floating, burden only particular tracts, and exclude executive rights, bonuses, and delay rentals. Never multiply an NPRI by the lease royalty until the instrument's language and controlling law establish that treatment. Have a landman assemble the recorded chain and counsel resolve ambiguous reservations. Require deed references, tract descriptions, depth limitations, and the exact fraction in the acquisition workbook. When the seller's decimal differs from the supported decimal by more than 1%, freeze pricing pending reconciliation; this is an internal threshold, not a title standard. The fallback is a smaller, verified acquisition or no purchase, rather than a speculative discount on ownership that may not exist.

The second cluster of traps hides between the courthouse index and the operator's pay deck: unprobated estates, omitted heirs, unreleased liens, marital-property claims, stale powers of attorney, and deeds that reserve the valuable depths. A division order is useful payment evidence but does not replace a title examination. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 addresses payment timing, qualifying withholding circumstances, and division orders; it does not make an operator's current decimal conclusive ownership proof. Pull certified instruments when the transaction requires them, search grantor and grantee variants, and reconcile every conveyance into the tract ledger. Use TexasFile or a county portal as a discovery aid, then preserve the underlying recorded document and retrieval date. Search applicable judgment, lien, and UCC records without assuming a UCC search establishes real property title. If a $40,000 purchase requires $6,000 of curative work, the economic basis starts at $46,000 before carrying costs; a hoped-for $50,000 exit leaves only $4,000 before selling expenses. Obtain executable curative deliverables before funding or use a negotiated escrow tied to specific releases. A seller's indemnity is only as useful as collectability and enforceability.

The third trap is treating every lease as the same royalty contract. Read the royalty valuation point, post-production cost language, affiliate-sale provisions, shut-in clauses, continuous development obligations, pooling authority, and depth or acreage release terms. A cost-free phrase does not automatically settle every deduction dispute; governing law and the entire instrument matter. Identify whether the operator can allocate compression, gathering, processing, or transportation charges and whether taxes are separately stated. An apparent $1,000 monthly gross entitlement with $180 of supported deductions and $70 of production taxes delivers $750, so valuing the asset at forty gross months rather than forty net months overstates that simple price anchor by $10,000. Those figures are illustrative underwriting inputs, not the portfolio scorecard. Obtain at least twelve production-month statements where available and flag any deduction ratio rising five percentage points above its trailing three-month median. That signal starts document review rather than proving misconduct. If lease language remains unresolved, model the disputed charge as payable, reserve investigation costs, and decline acquisitions whose margin depends on winning a future dispute. A cheap price cannot repair a defective valuation premise.

sections.heading: 2. Separate Docket Optionality from Producing Cash and Exit Liquidity
paragraphs: Pooling-docket curve-jumping fails when an application is treated as a completed well. Oklahoma Corporation Commission proceedings under 52 O.S. Section 87.1 can establish important spacing and pooling consequences, but a filing, hearing, order, election, permit, spud, completion, and first sale are different events. Track each event separately in the authorized agency portal and retain the actual order, not a broker screenshot. A simple illustrative acquisition pays $24,000 for an interest expected to receive $600 monthly after first sale. At an analyst-selected 10% annual carrying hurdle, an additional nine-month delay adds $1,800 of economic carrying burden before actual operating costs. The hurdle is a valuation assumption, not an invoice or a scorecard expense. More seriously, the well may never be drilled. Do not infer participation elections or cost-bearing obligations from a royalty label; determine exactly which interest is subject to the order and calendar its deadlines. If development slips ninety days beyond the documented investment milestone, stop follow-on purchases in that thesis and refresh the probability-weighted valuation. The fallback is pricing existing production alone, with unproved future drilling assigned no purchase premium.

Production forecasting creates another asymmetric loss when newcomers annualize a flush-production check, borrow against it, and ignore depletion. For an illustrative stress test, 100 monthly cash units declining to 65 and then 50 cannot support a flat 1,200-unit annual forecast. Build a monthly model by well and product using production history from the Texas Railroad Commission or the relevant state agency, operator statements, and a documented price deck. Enverus can assist where licensed, but its estimates do not replace the seller's actual ownership and settlement data. Separate oil, gas, and natural gas liquids; distinguish sales month from production month and inspect curtailments, workovers, and changed purchasers. A greater-than-20% volume decline against the same-well forecast for two reported months triggers an engineering refresh, after allowing for reporting lag and revisions. Pair that signal with a 25% realized-price downside and a six-month cash-delay test. Do not treat these internal thresholds as geological laws. Where debt requires distributions that the stressed net receipts cannot support, reduce leverage before purchase. The practical fallback is an unlevered position sized to survive interruption, not a covenant waiver assumed in advance.

Institutional flips break when a nonbinding indication becomes the only exit plan. Build a buyer-ready package containing tract schedules, recorded instruments, title exceptions, lease abstracts, well identifiers, ownership decimals, and reconciled receipts. In the institutional-flip play, purchasing for $80,000 and selling for $100,000 produces a $20,000 realized trading gain before $5,000 of separately expensed diligence and selling costs, leaving $15,000 before other overhead. The $80,000 returned acquisition basis is not operator revenue. If the buyer's final supported decimal is 15% smaller and the bid falls proportionally to $85,000, those same costs consume the entire spread. Track retrades by cause: ownership, price deck, lease burden, missing documents, or buyer liquidity. Pause repeat buying from a source when two consecutive packages suffer ownership-related price reductions above 5%. Negotiate defect procedures, cure periods, and narrowly defined surviving obligations rather than promising unlimited future reimbursements. The fallback is a hold case supported by current net royalties and available reserves. If that hold case fails, a fast-close discount does not justify buying an asset that only one uncommitted counterparty might accept.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Receipts Before Spending Cash That Can Be Recovered
paragraphs: A deposited royalty check can contain money the owner cannot safely distribute. Operator corrections may reverse duplicate payments, revise product prices, change allocated volumes, or apply an earlier ownership decimal. A title dispute can move future payments into suspense, while a purchaser correction can affect several prior production months. In the royalty reconciliation play, compare a supported 0.003125 decimal against a paid 0.003500 decimal on $100,000 of eligible monthly proceeds: the apparent excess is $37.50 monthly, or $450 across twelve identical months. Actual exposure requires statement-level reconstruction, not multiplication across unequal months. Isolate the apparent excess in the cash forecast, notify the operator through a documented channel, and obtain the contractual and factual basis for any proposed recovery. Do not presume either that every demand is valid or that a payment's age defeats recovery. Maintain a correction ledger showing production month, original statement, revised statement, asserted reason, disputed amount, and resolution. Any unexplained negative adjustment above 5% of trailing three-month receipts triggers distribution restraint and review. The fallback is distributing only reconciled cash while the disputed amount remains liquid and traceable.

Build the control around a four-way reconciliation: recorded ownership, operator decimal, product settlement, and bank cash. Use authorized EnergyLink downloads where available, operator remittance files, and a controlled spreadsheet or SQLite ledger keyed by owner number, property number, product, and production month. Preserve gross values, taxes, each deduction category, adjustments, and net paid separately. Bank deposits prove receipt, not correct calculation. Investigate any supported ownership mismatch immediately; use a $50 or 2% statement-to-bank variance, whichever is larger, as an internal triage threshold after grouping payments correctly. Monitor missing statements against the operator's established cycle and escalate payments thirty days beyond that cycle, while separately applying the jurisdiction's actual payment rules. Texas Natural Resources Code Sections 91.402 and 91.403 address payment timing and interest with specific exceptions; do not substitute the internal alert for statutory analysis. Automation should propose exceptions, not silently write off small mismatches. Repeated $20 errors across fifty properties total $1,000 per cycle. Route changed bank instructions through independent verification, and never send account credentials to a supposed operator representative merely because their email contains accurate well names.

Keep the canonical operating ledger separate from acquisition capital and illustrative deal examples. Conservative revenue is $30,000 with $24,000 of implied aggregate costs, leaving $6,000 at 20%; Base revenue is $215,000 with $145,125 of costs, leaving $69,875 at 32.5%; Scaled revenue is $400,000 with $220,000 of costs, leaving $180,000 at 45%. Revenue includes royalty receipts and realized rights-trading gains, excluding returned basis. Contractor counts describe a delivery bench, not three or four full-time salaries: Conservative and Base use one full-time person plus three contractors, while Scaled uses two plus four. The $1,000-$12,000 monthly opex range is not a complete allocation of every scenario's aggregate costs; do not force the annual cost residual into that range. The $15,000-$75,000 startup capital range and six-to-twenty-four-month first-deal window demand a separate liquidity schedule. In an illustrative flat-cost sensitivity, a $10,000 revenue reversal would move Conservative profit to a $4,000 loss; this does not alter its canonical case. Maintain distinct cash reserves for documented recoupment exposure, carrying costs, and upcoming tax obligations. Never describe underlying well sales or returned purchase principal as portfolio revenue.

sections.heading: 4. Stop Outreach Abuse, Data Bans, and Pooled-Capital Liability
paragraphs: The mapped play tcpa_litigator_scrub_honeypot_arbitrage is implemented here as consent-first screening, not a license to harass owners who lack litigation history. Lawful docket-derived risk signals may support review alongside mandatory applicable do-not-call checks, entity-specific suppression, revocation processing, and independently verified consent. Public mineral ownership does not establish telephone permission. Determine which federal and state calling rules apply to the actual campaign, technology, recipient, and purpose; a minerals purchase pitch cannot simply inherit another business's consent. The Telephone Consumer Protection Act, 47 U.S.C. Section 227, and 47 CFR Section 64.1200 govern relevant calling restrictions. Certain private actions under Section 227(b)(3) allow $500 per violation and discretionary trebling for willful or knowing violations; exposure depends on the specific facts and claim. Never treat that amount as a universal settlement price. An illustrative batch of 1,000 candidate records might leave 700 documented eligible contacts after all applicable checks; 300 are suppressed, not rerouted through fresh numbers. A $0.20 screening cost per candidate means $200 per batch, or about $0.286 per eligible record. This ancillary service illustration adds nothing to canonical mineral revenue.

A plaintiff-name match is a noisy risk signal, not a finding that someone is abusive or an authorization to contact everyone else. Common names, changed addresses, incomplete dockets, and mistaken party roles generate false matches. Use PACER or authorized court access within applicable terms, record provenance, minimize retained personal information, and restrict the service to documented campaign controls. Never create bait calls, impersonate a court, publish accusation lists, or suppress complaint handling because a recipient previously sued another caller. The fallback is explicit: disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks. Any missing permission evidence blocks that record in this consent-first workflow; any failed suppression synchronization pauses the campaign. Twilio and other communications providers apply their own acceptable-use and messaging requirements, separate from statutory duties. Rotating accounts after suspension, spoofing identity, sharing purchased credentials, or bypassing court access controls can produce termination and additional liability. A warning or material complaint cluster triggers investigation before sending resumes. Preserve provider notices, timestamps, and permission records; appeal through the legitimate process. No provider can promise permanent account access, and a replacement account does not cure the underlying conduct.

The final trap is financing a slow, disputed asset with promises that create immediate obligations. When pooling outside money, selling passive participations, or receiving compensation for placing interests, assess the actual structure before soliciting funds. Securities Act Section 2(a)(1), codified at 15 U.S.C. Section 77b(a)(1), expressly addresses fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its securities definition; other arrangements can also implicate investment-contract analysis. Section 5 registration requirements and any available exemption require transaction-specific work, while broker questions arise separately under Exchange Act Section 15(a). Calling investors club members or relabeling returns as royalty sharing does not decide the analysis. Require a documented offering path, accurate economics, proper custody arrangements, and clear authority over distributions before accepting outside capital. Track county mineral property taxes, reporting obligations, and applicable federal tax treatment separately from operator withholding. A $12,000 annual carrying budget requires $1,000 monthly reserving even during suspense. If fundraising authority, title, or liquidity remains unresolved, stop new commitments and preserve existing asset records. Survival comes from limiting irreversible obligations before chasing another apparently cheap acre.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in mineral rights, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (3–9 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: County-Record NMA and NPRI Origination, Pooling-Docket Signals, Royalty Verification, and Institutional Exit Demand
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps five operating plays: severed-title mineral acquisitions, NPRI purchases, producing-royalty acquisitions, pooling-docket curve-jumping, and institutional flips. Build the first three-to-ten wins over 3–9 months by connecting recorded ownership, operator activity, verified payment histories, and documented buyer demand. A one-owner, three-contractor pod concentrates diligence on opportunities that survive title, decline, price, and liquidity tests. Canonical annual owner profits are $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled; revenue counts royalty receipts and realized trading gains, never returned acquisition basis. The system below turns public signals into qualified owners, priced offers, completed purchases, and repeatable exits without treating a drilling application as a promised well.

sections.heading: 1. Map five acquisition plays to evidence, not acreage rumors
paragraphs: Start with one basin, two adjacent counties, and a written acquisition box that names formations, operators, interest types, check sizes, and maximum exposure to undeveloped acreage. The five mapped plays are operationally distinct: severed-title mineral acquisitions buy documented mineral ownership; NPRI purchases buy a defined nonparticipating royalty interest; producing-royalty acquisitions buy existing payment streams; pooling-docket curve-jumping buys before a public development signal becomes fully reflected in seller pricing; institutional flips aggregate or clarify interests for a documented downstream buyer. Net mineral acres, or NMA, measure ownership rather than identify a separate legal estate. An NPRI ordinarily lacks executive leasing rights, and its precise economic fraction depends on the instrument and applicable law. Assign each prospect one primary play and optional secondary tags so a producing tract near a new application does not become two pipeline opportunities. The owner runs sourcing and underwriting; a contract landman assembles ownership, an oil-and-gas attorney resolves instruments and closing terms, and a royalty accountant tests payment economics. That is the canonical 1 FT + 3 C pod, not four full-time salaries disguised as inexpensive automation. Concentration makes their limited hours useful.

Mine records in a sequence that preserves provenance. Begin with county clerk grantor-grantee indexes, recorded mineral deeds, reservations, probate filings, and assignments; use appraisal rolls only as discovery aids because assessed ownership does not establish the complete mineral chain. Connect legal descriptions to Railroad Commission of Texas GIS and drilling-permit records, or Oklahoma Corporation Commission imaging and case records when operating there. A permit, spacing application, pooling application, hearing notice, final order, spud report, completion report, and first production report are separate events with different certainty. Capture document date, retrieval date, docket identifier, applicant, formation, tract description, and current disposition in Airtable or a comparable searchable register. Link to the actual filing rather than a screenshot stripped of context. Enverus or another licensed data service can accelerate matching, but confirm material claims against primary records and license terms before redistribution. Reject acreage matches based solely on a common owner surname or a nearby well icon. The landman must connect the target estate to the correct tract and potentially relevant unit. A horizontal well crossing a map boundary does not establish that every nearby owner participates in its revenue.

Demand mining begins before an acquisition offer, not after closing. Interview ten credible mineral buyers and record their basin, county, formation, operator exclusions, minimum economic interest, producing-versus-undeveloped preference, documentation requirements, and typical review duration. Ask whether quoted prices assume clean title, current pay status, particular commodity prices, or a specified royalty burden. Request written acquisition criteria and refresh them monthly; a buyer's old purchase announcement is not current demand. Institutional flips work when the operator removes fragmentation, documentation friction, or lot-size mismatch that the buyer genuinely values. They fail when the operator merely adds a markup to the same incomplete package everyone else received. Build two plausible exits for each proposed flip, while underwriting the ability to hold the interest if neither buyer proceeds. Never describe an indicative bid as committed liquidity. Source direct owner purchases for the operator's account; compensated representation, solicitation for others, and certain assignments require a separate review of applicable licensing and transaction rules. For this chapter, a win means a completed acquisition or completed resale with reconciled settlement funds, not an introduction, unsigned expression of interest, or speculative buyer mandate.

callout.body: Veteran operators preserve the link between ownership, unit participation, payment economics, and a buyer's actual acquisition box.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify ownership, royalty economics, and downside before spending heavily
paragraphs: Use a 100-point qualification score that rewards evidence rather than excitement: ownership traceability earns 25 points, verified economics 25, development evidence 15, seller fit 15, and executable exit or holding capacity 20. Define anchors before scoring. Ownership earns its full allocation only when the chain, reservations, succession, and signing authority are sufficiently resolved for the proposed transaction; a tax-roll match earns five. Producing economics receive full points only with reconciled statements and a defensible decline model. Nonproducing interests instead require explicit probability, timing, commodity-price, and zero-development cases; do not award them producing cash-flow points. A score of 75 advances to attorney review, 60–74 returns to targeted research, and below 60 leaves the active queue. These are internal screening rules, not observed market success rates. Suspected identity fraud, an unresolved material title defect, or inadequate acquisition funding blocks an offer regardless of total score. Seller fit measures willingness, authority, timing, and documentation access, never presumed vulnerability. The owner reviews twenty lightweight prospects weekly but releases only two or three for paid deep diligence. Contractor costs otherwise consume the economics before the team has made its first defensible bid.

Calculate the economic interest independently before accepting the seller's acreage shorthand. If an owner holds an undivided one-quarter mineral interest in 80 gross acres, the holding represents 20 NMA. Under a simple acreage-based allocation to a 640-acre unit with a one-fifth lease royalty, the illustrative revenue decimal is 20 divided by 640, multiplied by 0.20, or 0.00625. Actual participation can differ because of unit terms, allocation methods, retained interests, production intervals, and instrument language. Do not reuse this calculation for an NPRI until counsel determines whether its fraction applies to gross production or to the lessor's royalty. Collect twelve-to-twenty-four months of statements where available and compare production months rather than check dates. Identify suspense releases, prior-period adjustments, minimum-payment accumulation, and purchaser changes. Reconcile operator-reported volumes with public production records while allowing for reporting delays and aggregation differences. Examine taxes and post-production deductions under the actual lease and governing law. A higher recent check can reflect price recovery, not improved reservoir performance. Underwrite each well cohort separately when new completions temporarily hide the decline of older production, and preserve the raw statements behind every modeled annual receipt.

Translate the score into a maximum cash commitment, not a claim that the asset is worth one precise number. Model a producing-interest downside with lower realized prices, faster decline, delayed payments, and no new wells; model undeveloped acreage with a genuinely unproductive outcome rather than an indefinitely postponed success. Deduct title work, legal review, recording, taxes, transaction expenses, and required holding liquidity from the acquisition budget. The canonical startup range is $15,000–$75,000, with monthly operating expense capacity of $1,000–$12,000; neither range authorizes tying up every dollar in deeds. For a $150,000 starting pool, an illustrative allocation of $100,000 acquisition cash, $20,000 diligence and closing capacity, and $30,000 liquidity keeps the uses explicit. This allocation is not an annual earnings scenario. Reject a transaction if the downside holding period exhausts cash needed for existing obligations. Texas Property Code § 5.021 supplies a foundational written-conveyance requirement; Texas Natural Resources Code § 91.402 governs covered payment timing and specified withholding circumstances. Neither replaces instrument-level review. Use local counsel for probate, marital interests, liens, entity authority, and recording requirements before treating the seller's signature as transferable ownership.

callout.body: An attractive screening score does not waive identity, ownership, economics, or capital verification.

Have counsel interpret the lease, reservations, NPRI fraction, and material burdens; resolve defects affecting the interest being priced.

sections.heading: 3. Run a respectful outbound cadence and an evidence-rich inbound funnel
paragraphs: Build a rolling cohort of 400 raw record observations, not a purchased list labeled mineral owners. Deduplicate spouses, trusts, estates, entities, and repeated docket appearances into an illustrative 240 distinct owner opportunities. Research may produce 80 qualified opportunities, 60 with a usable contact route, 24 substantive owner conversations, 12 document packages, eight written offers, four signed agreements, and three completed purchases. These planning assumptions imply a 0.75% raw-to-close yield and a 37.5% offer-to-close yield; they are testable starting hypotheses, not published industry benchmarks. Record both stage-entry dates and reasons for rejection so improved conversion does not merely reflect quietly dropping difficult leads from the denominator. Run this cohort across the 6–24 month first-deal horizon rather than promising a monthly acquisition cadence. Ten completed wins would require roughly 1,334 raw observations at the same assumed yield, with no assurance that yield persists as the county list becomes thinner. Track purchases and resales separately, and never count the same asset's acquisition and resale as two new sourced-owner wins. Paid diligence begins after meaningful qualification, keeping three contractors focused on evidence likely to change an actual bid.

Use a six-touch sequence over approximately 45 days, stopping immediately after a refusal or communication restriction. On day one, send a plain mailed introduction identifying the actual purchasing entity, the county, and the interest you want to discuss. On day seven, make a manual call only after checking applicable federal and state calling requirements and suppression records. On day fourteen, send a second letter with a short explanation of mineral versus royalty ownership. On day twenty-one, use individualized email only through an appropriate, lawfully obtained address and with required commercial-email information. On day thirty, offer a document checklist or scheduled call through the owner's preferred channel. On day forty-five, close the loop and explain how to recontact the buyer later. Avoid automated calls and unsolicited texts as the default; 47 CFR § 64.1200 and applicable state rules require channel-specific analysis. The opening message should say, 'We purchase mineral and royalty interests in this county; would you consider reviewing an offer for your interest?' Never imply operator affiliation, government authority, a mandatory response, or an impending loss of ownership. Store opt-outs centrally so contractors cannot accidentally restart a stopped sequence.

Inbound should answer a narrow owner's question rather than attract broad commodity speculation. Publish county-specific pages explaining what documents support a mineral offer, why a royalty decimal differs from acreage, and how producing and undeveloped interests are evaluated. Show a redacted sample document checklist and a clear purchasing-entity identity. Collect only contact details, county, interest type, and permission to discuss the property initially; request sensitive statements through a restricted-access upload after identity and relevance checks. Attribute each inquiry to its page, referral, mail campaign, or professional introduction. Respond within two business days, but do not price an asset from a form submission alone. Handle objections by exposing assumptions: when an owner says a neighbor received more, compare interest type, royalty burden, production, and transaction date. When they expect another well, show the filed evidence and separate the producing-only offer from any development increment. When they prefer monthly income, acknowledge that a sale exchanges future receipts for current cash and stop pushing if that trade does not fit. Professional referrals can include estate attorneys and accountants, but review compensation restrictions before offering referral payments or representing another party.

sections.heading: 4. Close the first wins without confusing sale proceeds with operating revenue
paragraphs: Convert a successful conversation into a bounded purchase process with a written interest description, price methodology, diligence period, permitted access to records, closing conditions, and responsibility for identified expenses. Counsel should distinguish a preliminary indication from a binding purchase agreement and ensure the deed conveys only the intended estate. Do not send an owner a broad mineral deed when the negotiated purchase covers only a defined royalty interest. Resolve title exceptions through specific curative documents rather than a spreadsheet note saying they are probably harmless. Verify payment instructions using independently established contact information; email threads alone are inadequate protection against diverted closing funds. Arrange the agreed recording and settlement sequence with the closing professional, then submit the operator's required ownership-transfer package. Recording does not instantly update the operator's pay deck. Track delivery, acknowledgment, requested documents, and the first statement under the new owner. Review division orders against the acquired interest rather than assuming the proposed decimal is correct. Texas Natural Resources Code § 91.402 provides relevant payment and division-order rules for covered interests, but the transaction still needs fact-specific review. A closed acquisition is a sourcing win; verified payment transfer is a separate operational milestone.

Keep the canonical scorecard separate from individual transaction illustrations. Conservative annual revenue is $30,000, with a 20% net margin and $6,000 owner profit; the implied expense envelope is $24,000. Base revenue is $215,000, with a 32.5% margin, $69,875 profit, and $145,125 of expenses. Scaled revenue is $400,000, with a 45% margin, $180,000 profit, and $220,000 of expenses. The revenue basis is royalty receipts plus realized rights-trading gains, excluding returned basis. An illustrative Base bridge could contain $120,000 of royalty receipts and a $155,000 rights resale carrying $60,000 of recoverable basis: the $95,000 gain plus receipts equals $215,000, not $275,000. This simplified bridge assumes no additional basis adjustments and places selling expenses in the expense envelope without double counting. Have the accountant reconcile the management presentation to tax and financial records. Acquisition cash recovered at resale is liquidity returned, not new operating earnings. Never count the operator's underlying oil-and-gas sales as the mineral owner's revenue. The monthly operating expense range does not cap total annual scenario expenses, which can include transaction-linked costs. Nor do scenario revenues specify how many acquisitions must close to achieve them.

Operate a weekly dashboard around evidence quality, capital exposure, and completed outcomes. Track distinct qualified owners, reachable contacts, substantive conversations, complete packages, written offers, signed agreements, completed purchases, and realized exits. Measure sourcing cost per qualified opportunity and total diligence cost per closed transaction, including failed files. Keep acquisition basis outside those acquisition-marketing ratios and maintain a separate deployed-capital schedule. Royalty reconciliation and production monitoring are the two canonical automation levers: automate imports, variance flags, reporting-date reminders, and document version tracking, not instrument interpretation or investment judgment. The owner reviews exceptions; the landman, attorney, and accountant receive bounded work orders with source links. Commodity prices, depletion, and title disputes remain material even after a workflow becomes efficient. The Scaled case uses 2 FT + 4 C, six people, rather than silently loading twice the work onto the original pod. If outside investors will pool funds, analyze the actual structure before solicitation: 15 U.S.C. § 77b(a)(1) expressly includes fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its securities definition. Do not assume that calling an arrangement a land purchase removes securities requirements. Expand only after completed files demonstrate repeatable sourcing, clean handoffs, and adequate holding liquidity.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, holds Rank #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score because capital, title work, and depletion constrain throughput. This chapter maps five operating plays: severed-mineral aggregation, NPRI yield acquisition, pooling-docket curve-jumping, royalty recovery, and institutional flips. A 1 FT + 3 C pod converts recorded instruments into reviewed ownership, controlled closings, and reconciled receipts using six executable SQLite reference modules. The mature-book 90-day walk separates $60,000 returned basis from $40,000 realized gain and reaches the Base annual run rate without counting sale proceeds twice. Canonical annual owner profits remain $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled. The controls target three recurring losses: buying the wrong interest, paying for speculative production, and treating unmatched cash as earned revenue.

sections.heading: 1. Convert Five Mineral Plays into One Capacity-Limited Deal Queue
paragraphs: Start with one economic-interest record, not one mailing-list row. The full-time principal owns pricing, capital allocation, seller communication, and the final cash tie-out. Three contractors provide land and title research, petroleum engineering, and bookkeeping; specialist counsel is purchased within the title contractor's scoped engagement rather than silently adding another permanent seat. Map each opportunity to five explicit work lanes: severed-mineral aggregation purchases fragmented NMA; NPRI yield acquisition buys documented nonparticipating royalty cash flows; pooling-docket curve-jumping prices public development changes; royalty recovery corrects receipts on owned interests; institutional flips assemble transferable packages for larger buyers. One parcel can serve several lanes, but it receives one asset identity and one allocated basis. Maintain separate gross acres, fractional mineral ownership, net mineral acres, royalty burden, depth limits, and effective dates. Never express an NPRI as NMA without preserving the instrument's actual royalty definition. An asset key combines jurisdiction, recorded vesting instrument, tract, depth interval, and interest fraction. A normalized seller name alone cannot establish ownership or prevent duplicate purchases. Cap simultaneous title examinations at the contractor's documented weekly capacity, and require a specific reason whenever the principal advances a lower-ranked file ahead of a complete one.

Build the ownership packet from county records before using a spreadsheet decimal to quote a price. Preserve deeds, reservations, probate orders, assignments, leases, amendments, and relevant pooling orders with document dates and retrieval provenance. Texas Property Code §13.001 makes recording status consequential for priority; recording a document does not independently establish that the grantor owned the interest conveyed. The title reviewer must resolve severances, executive rights, NPRI burdens, and depth restrictions against the specific conveyance. For a simple area-proportional unit with uniform ownership and no competing burdens, twenty NMA in a 640-acre unit at a one-fifth lease royalty produces a 0.00625 decimal: 20 divided by 640 multiplied by 0.20. That illustration is not a substitute for horizontal allocation language, tract participation factors, or an instrument-specific NPRI calculation. Compare the supported decimal with the operator's division-order decimal and investigate differences before signing. Use Texas RRC well and production records, Oklahoma Corporation Commission dockets, and county indexes as distinct evidence sources. Enverus or other licensed aggregators can accelerate screening, but an aggregator's ownership estimate never replaces the recorded chain. Store the exact downloaded artifact, not merely a search-results URL that may change next week.

Translate each lane into an explicit acquisition thesis and failure condition. Aggregation requires contiguous economic usefulness to a buyer, not simply many small deeds. NPRI yield underwriting requires lease-specific deduction treatment and a defensible production forecast. Docket curve-jumping requires a public filing, tract match, procedural status, and pricing that survives delayed drilling; a pooling application is neither a completed well nor a royalty payment. Recovery work requires an owned receivable supported by statements, not a projected benefit counted immediately as revenue. An institutional flip requires transferable title, a buyer's document checklist, and enough spread after acquisition basis and selling costs. The engineer builds a monthly decline case using well age, downtime, product mix, realized differentials, deductions, and plausible abandonment timing. The principal then prices the asset against a delayed-development case rather than paying today's price for an optimistic permit narrative. Allocate contractor hours to exceptions: disputed title, anomalous decimals, and material forecast variance. Routine data collection should be batched. The canonical 6–24 month time to first deal remains the startup expectation; the later 90-day example describes a mature book and prepared pipeline, not an accelerated promise for a new entrant. Rejecting an attractive headline yield is productive when its title or depletion assumptions cannot survive examination.

sections.heading: 2. Build the Six-Module Ledger Before Increasing Acquisition Volume
paragraphs: Use the six reference modules in table order as one Python 3.9 script. They depend only on the standard library and initialize an isolated in-memory SQLite ledger; choose a durable local file through open_ledger when implementing the reviewed design. Keep SQLite on a local filesystem, use one connection per worker, and serialize mutations with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Concurrent writers either acquire the write lock or fail without a partial commit. UNIQUE constraints protect source identities and economic-interest identities, while request hashes reject a reused key carrying different data. Workflow updates additionally compare both the expected version and current stage. These controls eliminate check-then-write races within the reference mutation paths; they do not turn direct database access into an authenticated application. Restrict filesystem access, expose only authorized operations, and preserve reviewed deployment migrations. A timeout is a retryable failure using the identical event key, never permission to generate a replacement transaction identity. Hash the actual evidence artifact before registration and retain its retrievable location in the surrounding document index. The reference stores the digest and reviewer, not private deed contents. Immutable audit rows detect accidental mutation; separately retained backups are still necessary against database replacement or privileged tampering.

The ledger uses integer cents and balanced account pairs rather than binary floating-point amounts or an editable revenue total. Each journal row contains one equal debit and credit, and every cash event plus all associated rows commits atomically. An acquisition debits asset basis and credits cash. A profitable sale credits basis only for the retired investment and credits trading gain for the excess; a below-basis sale separately records rights loss. The implementation deliberately supports complete-lot dispositions, so a partial assignment must first receive a reviewed allocation design rather than slipping through an unsupported parameter. Opening contributed assets and equity funding are balance-sheet entries, not operator revenue. The management view recognizes supported royalty receipts on collection and realized sale gains on settlement. Maintain a separate tax and accrual workpaper for depletion, withholding, receivables, and jurisdiction-specific treatment; 26 U.S.C. §§611–612 make depletion and adjusted basis substantive accounting topics. Successful acquisition costs that belong in basis must be included in the acquired lot's recorded amount. The cohort's separate prospect costs concern abandoned searches and screening rather than the purchased lot. This distinction keeps the sale spread, operating expenses, and returned investment from being counted inconsistently.

Treat workflow state as evidence of an operational decision, not as an instruction to move money. SCORED means the screening inputs passed a routing threshold; VERIFIED requires reviewed title and underwriting artifacts; ESCROW requires escrow instructions; CLOSED requires the completed closing packet. The reference makes no external payment calls and therefore cannot create a bank-side retry race. Record a settlement only after independent bank and escrow evidence establishes its occurrence. If a later integration initiates payments, add a durable outbox, a provider-supported idempotency key, and status recovery before enabling dispatch; a local SQL transaction alone cannot ensure exactly-once external effects. The QA module creates its own database, exercises replay and conflict behavior, retires the sold basis, and checks quarterly revenue, expenses, profit, and ending cash. It is a runnable fixture, not evidence that an installed system has passed testing. Extend deployment tests with two independent connections contending for the same transition and transaction key, process interruption before commit, and restoration from backup. The bookkeeper owns exception reports; the principal owns clearing them. Retain the original bank transaction identifier as the source key so reimporting a statement cannot manufacture another receipt.

def intake(source_key, asset_key, title_packet, operator_match,
           docket_match, price_buffer):
    flags = (title_packet, operator_match, docket_match, price_buffer)
    if any(type(value) is not bool for value in flags):
        raise ValueError("screening inputs must be explicit booleans")
    if not source_key.strip() or not asset_key.strip():
        raise ValueError("stable source and canonical asset keys required")
    payload = [source_key, asset_key] + list(flags)
    digest = fingerprint(payload)
    score = sum(
        weight for weight, passed in zip((30, 25, 20, 25), flags)
        if passed
    )
    stage = "SCORED" if score >= 70 else "REJECTED"
    with atomic():
        prior = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM deal WHERE source_key = ?", (source_key,)
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior["request_hash"] != digest:
                raise ValueError("intake replay changed its payload")
            return prior["deal_id"]
        deal_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO deal VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1)",
            (deal_id, source_key, asset_key, digest, stage, score)
        )
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO workflow_event VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            ("intake:" + source_key, deal_id, digest, "NEW", stage, 1)
        )
        return deal_id

VIEWS = """
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS ledger_legs AS
SELECT source_key, debit_account AS account,
       amount_cents AS signed_cents
FROM journal
UNION ALL
SELECT source_key, credit_account AS account,
       -amount_cents AS signed_cents
FROM journal;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS monthly_reconciliation AS
SELECT substr(e.effective_date, 1, 7) AS month,
       SUM(CASE WHEN l.account = 'cash'
           THEN l.signed_cents ELSE 0 END) AS cash_change_cents,
       -SUM(CASE WHEN l.account IN ('royalty_revenue','trading_gain')
           THEN l.signed_cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
       SUM(CASE WHEN l.account IN ('opex','deal_cost','rights_loss')
           THEN l.signed_cents ELSE 0 END) AS expense_cents,
       -SUM(CASE WHEN l.account IN (
           'royalty_revenue','trading_gain','opex',
           'deal_cost','rights_loss'
       ) THEN l.signed_cents ELSE 0 END) AS profit_cents
FROM ledger_legs l
JOIN cash_event e USING(source_key)
GROUP BY substr(e.effective_date, 1, 7);
"""

def install_views():
    db.executescript(VIEWS)

def bank_tieout(bank_closing_cents):
    if type(bank_closing_cents) is not int:
        raise ValueError("bank balance must use integer cents")
    book = db.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(signed_cents), 0) "
        "FROM ledger_legs WHERE account = 'cash'"
    ).fetchone()[0]
    return {
        "book_cents": book,
        "bank_cents": bank_closing_cents,
        "difference_cents": book - bank_closing_cents,
    }

install_views()

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)

def expect_value_error(action):
    try:
        action()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected a refused operation")

def fixture_closed_deal(label):
    deal_id = intake(
        "fixture-source:" + label, "fixture-asset:" + label,
        True, True, True, True
    )
    for kind in ("title", "underwriting", "escrow", "closing"):
        register_evidence(
            deal_id, kind, fingerprint(["fixture", label, kind]),
            "fixture reviewer"
        )
    for version, target in enumerate(
        ("VERIFIED", "ESCROW", "CLOSED"), 1
    ):
        advance(label + ":" + target, deal_id, version, target)
    return deal_id

def run_qa():
    global db
    original = db
    db = open_ledger()
    try:
        install_views()
        legacy = fixture_closed_deal("legacy")
        lot = fixture_closed_deal("cohort-one")
        post("fixture:funding", "2026-12-31", "funding", 10000000)
        post("fixture:legacy", "2026-12-31", "opening_asset",
             15000000, legacy)
        post("fixture:purchase", "2027-01-15", "purchase",
             6000000, lot)
        for month, royalty, prospect_cost in (
            ("01", 400000, 300000),
            ("02", 450000, 300000),
            ("03", 525000, 328125),
        ):
            post("fixture:royalty:" + month, "2027-" + month + "-28",
                 "royalty", royalty, legacy)
            post("fixture:opex:" + month, "2027-" + month + "-28",
                 "opex", 900000)
            post("fixture:prospects:" + month,
                 "2027-" + month + "-28", "deal_cost", prospect_cost)
        post("fixture:sale", "2027-03-20", "sale",
             10000000, lot, 6000000)
        count = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM journal").fetchone()[0]
        post("fixture:sale", "2027-03-20", "sale",
             10000000, lot, 6000000)
        require(
            db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM journal").fetchone()[0]
            == count, "cash replay created extra entries"
        )
        expect_value_error(
            lambda: post("fixture:sale", "2027-03-20", "sale",
                         10000001, lot, 6000000)
        )
        expect_value_error(
            lambda: post("fixture:second-sale", "2027-03-21", "sale",
                         10000000, lot, 6000000)
        )
        expect_value_error(
            lambda: advance("fixture:stale", lot, 1, "VERIFIED")
        )
        require(
            advance("cohort-one:CLOSED", lot, 3, "CLOSED") == 4,
            "workflow replay changed its recorded result"
        )
        rows = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM monthly_reconciliation "
            "WHERE month BETWEEN '2027-01' AND '2027-03' "
            "ORDER BY month"
        ).fetchall()
        require(
            [row["cash_change_cents"] for row in rows]
            == [-6800000, -750000, 9296875],
            "monthly cash movement mismatch"
        )
        revenue = sum(row["revenue_cents"] for row in rows)
        expenses = sum(row["expense_cents"] for row in rows)
        profit = sum(row["profit_cents"] for row in rows)
        require(revenue == 5375000, "quarter revenue mismatch")
        require(expenses == 3628125, "quarter cost mismatch")
        require(profit == 1746875, "quarter profit mismatch")
        require(revenue * 4 == 21500000, "annual revenue mismatch")
        require(profit * 4 == 6987500, "annual owner profit mismatch")
        require(profit * 1000 == revenue * 325, "margin mismatch")
        require(asset_balance(lot) == 0, "sold lot retained basis")
        require(asset_balance(legacy) == 15000000,
                "legacy asset basis changed")
        require(bank_tieout(11746875)["difference_cents"] == 0,
                "closing bank balance mismatch")
        require(
            db.execute(
                "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(signed_cents), 0) FROM ledger_legs"
            ).fetchone()[0] == 0,
            "double-entry trial balance mismatch"
        )
        require(
            not db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall(),
            "foreign key integrity failure"
        )
        return {
            "quarter_revenue_cents": revenue,
            "quarter_profit_cents": profit,
            "closing_cash_cents": 11746875,
        }
    finally:
        db.close()
        db = original

sections.heading: 3. Execute Closing, Production Monitoring, and Receipt Recovery Without Losing the Chain
paragraphs: Before any wire, the principal reviews a compact closing packet with the purchase agreement, conveyance, ownership schedule, resolved exceptions, settlement statement, and independently verified payee instructions. The land contractor confirms that the deed's legal description and reserved rights match the priced interest, including depths and effective dates. The engineer confirms that the acquired interval actually participates in the modeled wells. The bookkeeper checks that allocated purchase basis equals the closing schedule and that no earlier event already recorded the same settlement. Verify changed wire instructions using an established contact channel, not the telephone number inside the change request. Record conveyances promptly under the applicable county process and preserve acceptance and instrument numbers. Escrow release conditions must identify the required executed instruments and delivery evidence; a generic email saying title is clean is insufficient. Existing tax liens, probate limitations, and conflicting assignments require issue-specific resolution. The four-person pod stays efficient by presenting one indexed exception schedule rather than circulating multiple contradictory checklists. No participant should silently change the purchased fraction after pricing. A material scope change returns the file to reviewed underwriting and a documented revised agreement before the external closing proceeds.

After closing, submit the operator's ownership-transfer package and track each payor's acknowledgment, required tax form, division-order status, and suspense reason. Texas Natural Resources Code §91.402 specifies payment timing with enumerated circumstances permitting withholding; §91.403 addresses interest on late payments subject to its terms. Build jurisdiction-specific deadline fields instead of applying a universal countdown. Royalty automation should normalize payor, property, API identifier, product, production month, decimal, volume, price, deductions, tax withholding, and net remittance. Oil and gas measurement units must remain explicit. Match the statement total to the deposit, then explain allocation differences across properties. The reference general ledger records the supported collected amount; its statement subledger must preserve gross-to-net detail for later accounting classification. Use EnergyLink where the payor supports it, and retain the original statement rather than trusting an extracted CSV alone. Reconciliation exceptions should distinguish missing statements, duplicate deposits, stale ownership, decimal disagreement, and revised production periods. A recovery estimate remains an exception balance until the payor resolves it and the relevant receipt arrives. This prevents the royalty-recovery play from inflating the same month's cash, revenue, and projected sale value simultaneously.

Run production monitoring monthly, but route only material exceptions to the engineer. Compare observed volumes with the acquisition forecast after aligning reporting months and accounting for revisions. A lower royalty check can reflect price, downtime, deductions, payment lag, or ownership changes; it does not automatically prove reservoir decline. Preserve forecast versions and document whether a change alters hold value, sale timing, or reserve cash. Institutional buyers should receive an indexed package containing the supported interest schedule, recorded instruments, payor history, production series, deductions analysis, and unresolved exceptions. Avoid advertising a pooling application as booked production. Before a flip closes, reconcile the sale perimeter to the acquisition lot and confirm that the ledger can retire exactly that basis; partial dispositions need an allocation extension outside the reference implementation. If outside capital is pooled, evaluate the offering structure before soliciting investors: 15 U.S.C. §77b(a)(1) includes fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its security definition. An entity wrapper does not itself settle the analysis. Keep asset operations separate from investor subscriptions and distributions, and obtain a structure-specific review before accepting funds.

sections.heading: 4. Walk a Mature 90-Day Cohort from Lead Scrubs to Base-Case Cash
paragraphs: The worked cohort begins after the business has established a producing book and a prepared acquisition pipeline. Opening assets are $100,000 unrestricted cash and $150,000 contributed mineral basis, representing $250,000 of capital within the canonical $15,000–$75,000 startup range. Opening equity is not revenue. The existing book produces collected royalties of $4,000, $4,500, and $5,250 across three months. Month 1 also closes a fully prepared $60,000 mineral lot, including its capitalizable acquisition costs; Month 3 sells the entire lot for $100,000. Its $60,000 returned basis replenishes capital, while only the $40,000 realized gain enters scorecard revenue. The 54 newly logged leads support continuing pipeline work, but the illustration does not assert that cold intake produced a fully reviewed institutional exit inside ninety days. The purchased lot belongs to Month 1's tracked cohort because its closing enters this operating window; its preparation predates the window. Use explicit origination, intake, verification, purchase, and sale dates in the operating workbook so a fast closing cannot conceal a long development history. The ledger fixture models the existing book and closed lot; the cohort register separately tracks unpurchased prospects.

Month 1 logs eighteen opportunities: nine fail initial screening, six fail documented title review, two remain repricing files, and one prepared lot closes. Month 2 logs eighteen more: nine fail screening, six remain in title remediation, and three enter the bid queue without a purchase commitment. Month 3 logs eighteen: ten fail screening, five remain in title remediation, and three enter the bid queue. These dispositions total 54 without inventing additional acquisitions. Rejected prospects have no acquired asset basis; their actual search expense remains visible. Each month carries $9,000 recurring operating expense, within the canonical $1,000–$12,000 monthly opex range. Additional abandoned-prospect and screening costs are $3,000, $3,000, and $3,281.25. Those costs are separate from recurring opex and from the purchased lot's capitalized basis. The resulting quarter has $27,000 recurring opex plus $9,281.25 prospect expense, totaling $36,281.25. The principal and three contractors must fit their actual workload and charges inside those budgets; the headcount labels do not create free specialist capacity. The quarter's cash low point is $24,500 at Month 2 close, before the institutional buyer's settlement replenishes liquidity.

Reconcile the quarter in two independent directions. Revenue is $13,750 collected royalties plus $40,000 realized trading gain, totaling $53,750. Subtract $36,281.25 costs to obtain $17,468.75 owner profit, exactly 32.5% of recognized revenue. Cash starts at $100,000, receives $13,750 royalties and $100,000 sale proceeds, and pays $60,000 acquisition basis plus $36,281.25 costs, ending at $117,468.75. The acquired and sold lot has zero remaining basis; the opening mineral book retains $150,000 before separately assessed depletion adjustments. Four equivalent operating quarters produce $215,000 revenue, $145,125 costs, and $69,875 annual owner net profit. This is a run-rate reconciliation, not a claim that seasonal receipts or institutional closings arrive evenly. If the sale slips beyond Day 90, the same quarter ends with $17,468.75 cash, $60,000 unsold lot basis, and a $22,531.25 operating loss before any impairment assessment. No projected exit gain fills that gap. Preserve this liquidity stress alongside the canonical Conservative $6,000, Base $69,875, and Scaled $180,000 annual profit cases. Scaling to 2 FT + 4 C requires additional verified throughput, not counting returned principal as higher revenue.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, holds Rank #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps the tooling stack to five operator plays: severed-title acquisitions, NPRI cash-flow purchases, pooling-docket curve-jumping, owned-asset royalty recovery, and institutional flips. County instruments establish the ownership evidence; state production systems and hearing dockets expose changes; licensed datasets accelerate screening without replacing source documents. A 1 FT + 3 C pod needs reproducible joins, exception queues, and acquisition-specific evidence packets rather than another oversized dashboard. Canonical annual owner profits remain $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled. Revenue means royalty receipts plus realized rights-trading gains, excluding returned basis. The directory distinguishes access costs, source latency, extraction restraint, and practical fallbacks so automation improves decisions without manufacturing title certainty.

sections.heading: 1. Build a source hierarchy that distinguishes ownership from operating signals
paragraphs: Start with five explicit queues, not a universal parcel scraper. Severed-title acquisitions need county conveyances and tract interpretation; NPRI cash-flow purchases need the creating instrument, lease terms, and payment evidence; pooling-docket curve-jumping needs applications, hearing changes, and signed orders; owned-asset royalty recovery needs statements and production comparisons; institutional flips need transferable evidence and clean provenance. These are the chapter's five operating mappings, not five extra revenue streams. Assign the full-time principal to pricing, seller decisions, and capital allocation. Use three contractors for land/title research, petroleum and production analysis, and data/reconciliation work, with counsel engaged within the land/title scope when interpretation requires it. Contractor counts describe functional coverage, not three full-time salaries. Restrict the initial footprint to one basin and a manageable county set. A recorded instrument can establish a link in ownership but may omit earlier reservations; a tax roll can identify a mailing lead but cannot establish the mineral estate. An operator's division order can support payment reconciliation without curing title. Encode these distinctions in source types so a mailing address, production observation, and ownership conclusion never share the same confidence label. Every queued opportunity needs a named reviewer and a next evidence request.

Acquire evidence from the most authoritative source available for the question being answered. For Texas, county clerk records supply deeds and assignments, while Railroad Commission systems supply well, lease, completion, and reported production records. Texas production often arrives at lease level, so a lease total cannot automatically become one horizontal well's revenue forecast. Oklahoma Corporation Commission imaging and electronic case records support separate operating and pooling investigations; an application is neither a final order nor proof that the target interest participates. New Mexico OCD well files and hearing materials require the same distinction between requested relief and executed development. BLM MLRS adds federal land-status and case context, while ONRR public datasets provide aggregate revenue context rather than an individual's royalty ledger. Commercial products shorten the search path, but licensing, coverage, export rights, and historical depth determine usefulness. Ask each vendor for a trial using twenty already-researched tracts and a written description of correction handling. Measure missed wells, duplicated laterals, stale operator names, and title documents that cannot be reproduced. Prefer a narrower feed with traceable timestamps over broad coverage whose fields conceal their origin. Keep the trial findings alongside the purchase decision.

Treat the directory's latency descriptions as source characteristics and desk polling choices, not promised publication schedules. Before enabling a connector, record its actual access terms, permitted automation, advertised limits, export format, and responsible contact. Public search access does not imply unrestricted bulk retrieval, and a free portal does not make certified copies free. When a documented API exists, use the licensed endpoint and the provider's current authentication instructions; otherwise use an authorized export or a human download rather than reverse-engineering private application calls. Set one worker per host until documented limits justify more, honor Retry-After, apply bounded exponential backoff, and cache immutable instrument images by content digest. Poll active dockets each business day where permitted, but refresh monthly production after each observed reporting release and revisit revisions. Capture both the reporting period and retrieval time. A portal outage should create a visible stale-source flag, not silently extend yesterday's values into today's underwriting. Maintain a county clerk request path and a regulator records contact before depending on any feed. This modest discipline gives a four-person pod durable coverage without turning retrieval failures into speculative acquisition signals or spending contractor hours repairing avoidable duplicate downloads.

sections.heading: 2. Turn mixed records into a tract-centered, auditable enrichment waterfall
paragraphs: Use a tract-centered model with separate entities for instruments, parties, interests, wells, units, leases, docket events, and payments. Store the source's identifier unchanged alongside a normalized search key. API well identifiers must remain strings so leading zeroes survive; preserve sidetrack and completion suffixes where supplied instead of collapsing every record to one borehole. Texas district-and-lease identifiers belong in their own namespace. County instrument numbers require county and recording jurisdiction, because the same number can recur elsewhere. Represent an interest as a dated assertion linked to supporting instruments, not a permanent percentage attached to a person's name. Separate mineral ownership, executive rights, lease royalty, NPRI burden, depth limitations, and tract participation. For illustration, forty gross acres multiplied by a one-quarter mineral ownership fraction equals ten NMA; it does not determine the royalty decimal without lease and allocation terms. An NPRI can be fixed or floating depending on the instrument and governing interpretation, so a single generic royalty multiplier is unsafe. Keep geometry provenance and coordinate reference systems explicit. A wellbore crossing a polygon supports a spatial investigation, not a conclusion about unit allocation, effective pooling, or the seller's transferable interest. Require a reviewer to resolve those relationships.

Build the enrichment waterfall around increasing evidence cost. First normalize a seller-supplied legal description and search the county index for the creating and latest relevant instruments. Second connect the tract to regulator wells, leases, and units using identifiers and documented spatial relationships. Third retrieve docket materials for pending activity and distinguish application, continuance, hearing, and signed-order states. Fourth enrich with licensed production history and commercial interpretations only where those fields reduce a specific underwriting uncertainty. Fifth request seller statements, division orders, leases, and tax documents to reconcile actual ownership and cash receipts. Stop paid enrichment when a fatal reservation or excluded depth makes the target unbuyable. Maintain name variants, trust names, estates, and entity successors as candidate links until instruments support consolidation. An assessor mailing address is a contact clue, not proof that the addressee owns minerals. Use official entity records and seller confirmation before relying on a business-name match. Avoid broad personal-data purchases when a narrow county search answers the question. Log each match's basis, competing candidates, reviewer, and unresolved conflict. The principal should see the next cheapest decisive evidence request, not a decorative confidence percentage generated from loosely matched names.

Implement a small append-only evidence store before adding orchestration software. Python's urllib.request, csv, json, sqlite3, hashlib, decimal, and logging modules cover authorized HTTP retrieval, structured exports, local indexing, checksums, money arithmetic, and run records. Keep original files outside the working tables, store their SHA-256 digests, and record source URL, retrieval time, document date, reporting period, parser version, and access entitlement. PDF image extraction may require a separately installed desktop OCR product; its output remains a searchable derivative, never the controlling deed text. Save corrections as new observations with links to the superseded record. Make ingestion idempotent using source identity plus document digest or a documented observation key, not filename alone. Test fixtures should include duplicate downloads, revised production, missing pages, leading-zero identifiers, and one deliberately conflicting ownership chain. Export a narrow review workbook for the land contractor rather than requiring everyone to operate the database. Back up the evidence store and test restoration to a separate directory. The data contractor owns failed imports; the land contractor owns title exceptions; the production contractor owns allocation and decline questions. This division prevents software repairs from silently becoming substantive ownership decisions during a rushed bid.

callout.body: Spend contractor hours on interpretation and exceptions; use retrieval automation to preserve the evidence that makes those judgments reproducible.
items: Search deed references backward before paying for owner enrichment; the operative reservation often sits several instruments before the seller's acquisition.
Keep Texas lease production separate from well-level forecasts; ask the production contractor to explain any allocation across multiple producing wells.
Track OCC cause numbers through continuances and signed orders; a rescheduled hearing changes the timing thesis without changing the tract itself.
Save the exact exhibit and page supporting each institutional-buyer claim; a concise evidence index can shorten repeated diligence requests.

sections.heading: 3. Diagnose false signals before converting observations into bids or recovery claims
paragraphs: The highest-value diagnostic is a contradiction queue. Compare new production against the prior reported vintage, not just against the previous month, because amended reports can create false growth. Flag zero-to-positive transitions, sharp volume changes, operator changes, and new completion filings for review, while distinguishing shut-ins, workovers, meter adjustments, and first sales. Keep oil, gas, and water units separate; do not add barrels to Mcf or treat a gas conversion convention as a contractual payment factor. A benchmark price from EIA is context, not the operator's realized sale price after quality, location, and contract effects. For pooling-docket curve-jumping, monitor the tract's relationship to requested spacing and pooling relief, applicant identity, notice evidence, hearing disposition, order terms, and subsequent development. Receiving a docket alert creates a research task, not proof of imminent cash flow. If a filed exhibit and a commercial map disagree, retain both and resolve the underlying survey or legal-description issue. Use the land contractor for ownership and order interpretation, the production contractor for timing and allocation, and the principal for the bid ceiling. That separation stops optimistic event narratives from flowing directly into price assumptions without a reviewed evidentiary bridge.

Royalty reconciliation starts with the asset's documented payment decimal and statement structure. In a simplified illustration with uniform unit treatment, ten NMA inside a 640-acre unit under a one-fifth lease royalty produces a 0.003125 decimal before other burdens or contractual adjustments. If the applicable sales volume is 10,000 barrels at $70 per barrel, multiplying $700,000 by that decimal yields $2,187.50 before applicable deductions and taxes. This is an interest-math illustration, not an addition to the canonical revenue cases. Actual allocation can differ for horizontal wells, tract factors, effective dates, and NPRI language. Match statement lines by property, product, production month, sale month, and adjustment references. Separate gross value, deductions, withholding, suspense releases, and prior-period corrections so a larger check does not masquerade as improved reservoir performance. Under Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402, payment timing and withholding conditions require fact-specific review; a delayed payment is not automatically wrongful. Prepare a recovery inquiry with statement extracts, supporting instruments, a decimal calculation, and the precise disputed period. Log the operator's response and any corrected payment. Count recovered receipts only once, when recognized under the desk's consistent accounting policy, rather than treating the demand amount as earned revenue.

Instrument and spatial diagnostics matter as much as payment arithmetic. Run duplicate-document checks, page-count comparisons, and OCR spot checks on fractions, exceptions, depth clauses, and exhibit references. A scanned one-eighth can be misread as one-third, and an omitted exhibit can remove the only precise tract description. QGIS can reveal invalid polygons, coordinate-system mismatches, or lateral paths that appear shifted after an incorrect transformation; it cannot interpret a reservation or resolve conflicting surveys. Validate intersections against recorded descriptions and appropriate survey evidence. For institutional flips, create a buyer-facing source index that identifies what the buyer can independently retrieve and what requires a separate license. Do not redistribute commercial datasets merely because the desk purchased access. Keep seller tax documents, bank details, and personal identifiers out of general review exports; use restricted storage and share only material needed for the transaction. Apply the same restraint to contractor access. Before outreach or data-room publication, have the principal confirm recipients and the intended disclosure scope. A clean packet should expose unresolved questions plainly, not bury them behind composite scores. The objective is a defensible interest and a reproducible cash explanation, not a visually persuasive map with unsupported ownership labels.

sections.heading: 4. Fund the stack from canonical economics and operate a four-person exception desk
paragraphs: The scorecard is the operating boundary, not a target to rewrite with optimistic automation savings. Conservative revenue is $30,000 at a 20% net margin, producing $6,000 annual owner profit and implying $24,000 of total annual expenses. Base revenue is $215,000 at 32.5%, producing $69,875 and implying $145,125 of expenses. Scaled revenue is $400,000 at 45%, producing $180,000 and implying $220,000 of expenses. Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C. Do not subtract a new software budget from these profits and still claim the same canonical scenario. Instead allocate any proposed subscription inside its existing expense envelope or show a separately labeled sensitivity. For example, a $6,000 annual data package would consume one-quarter of the Conservative expense envelope before title work, administration, or other costs. A free-source pilot is therefore a sensible starting posture, not an assertion that diligence is free. The stated $1,000–$12,000 monthly opex range is a planning band, not a promise that every scenario's total annual expenses equal twelve times recurring overhead. Transaction-specific costs and accounting classifications still need explicit treatment in the desk ledger.

Keep capital deployment, cash proceeds, and recognized revenue in separate views. The stated $15,000–$75,000 startup capital range primarily describes the ability to buy and hold rights while research and payment cycles unfold; it is not operator revenue. In an illustrative flip, an interest purchased for $100,000 and sold for $130,000 produces $130,000 of sale proceeds, including $100,000 of returned basis and a $30,000 realized gain before separately modeled transaction costs. Only the gain belongs in the scorecard's rights-trading revenue component, with expense treatment kept consistent. Record royalty receipts separately and prevent a recovered payment from appearing in both ordinary receipts and a second recovery line. For institutional flips, preserve a basis schedule by acquired interest and track partial disposals so the remaining asset does not inherit an arbitrary zero basis. Never value the desk by the underlying operator's gross hydrocarbon sales or the buyer's total portfolio capital. The six-to-twenty-four-month first-deal window also means a promising research pipeline can coexist with limited near-term receipts. Track cash runway, committed purchase capital, research spend, and delayed payments alongside the profit model. Automation reduces clerical friction but cannot eliminate commodity exposure, depletion, or title disputes.

Run a weekly evidence meeting with one page per live opportunity and a strict exception agenda. The data contractor reports failed imports, stale sources, and revised records; the land contractor reports ownership breaks and docket changes; the production contractor reports volume, allocation, and decline concerns; the principal resolves spend and bid decisions. Measure instrument retrieval time, reviewed matches per paid hour, material exceptions caught before bidding, statement lines reconciled, and buyer questions answered from existing evidence. Avoid optimizing raw lead count when title research is the bottleneck. Promote a paid feed only after a basin-specific pilot demonstrates saved review hours or a documented reduction in costly misses, with both effects evaluated inside the canonical expense envelope. Recheck access terms and source coverage at renewal. If raising pooled capital, evaluate the proposed structure against securities definitions and applicable offering requirements before soliciting investors; fractional mineral interests and investment contracts require careful analysis under 15 U.S.C. Section 77b(a)(1). Texas recording priorities under Property Code Section 13.001 and federal communitization under 30 U.S.C. Section 226(m) likewise belong in targeted transaction review, not generic software labels. The winning small desk maintains a shorter distance between source evidence, specialist judgment, and an economically disciplined decision.
