chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: attractive asset economics, constrained by capital, title work, and specialist labor. This chapter maps five operator plays: producing-mineral acquisitions, NPRI acquisitions, pooling-docket curve-jumping, royalty reconciliation, and institutional flips. Each requires different authority, contract language, and evidence before money moves. The Conservative, Base, and Scaled cases produce annual owner net profits of $6,000, $69,875, and $180,000 on recognized revenue of $30,000, $215,000, and $400,000. Returned acquisition basis never becomes revenue. Build the initial operation around one full-time principal and three specialist contractors; reserve the six-person structure for the Scaled case. Use state-specific title review, narrow service engagements, documented outreach, and separate securities analysis before accepting pooled investor capital.

sections.heading: 1. Classify the Interest, Jurisdiction, and Actual Operator Role
paragraphs: Begin every opportunity with an interest classification, not a price per acre. A fee mineral interest can carry executive, bonus, rental, and royalty rights, but prior reservations may separate those attributes. An NPRI normally lacks executive rights and participation in bonuses or rentals; its actual language determines whether the royalty is fixed or floats with the lease royalty. A deed conveying one sixteenth of production does not necessarily convey one sixteenth of the lessor's royalty. Have the title attorney resolve that distinction before the principal converts acres into cash flow. For this chapter, the five mapped plays are producing-mineral acquisitions, NPRI acquisitions, pooling-docket curve-jumping, royalty reconciliation, and institutional flips. Maintain a separate rights-and-authority sheet for each play, including tract description, recording references, ownership fraction, lease status, executive holder, and permitted activity. Texas Property Code Chapter 13 makes recording and notice relevant to competing claims; a county index search alone does not establish marketable title. Obtain the underlying instruments, probate documents, assignments, releases, and applicable judgments. The principal owns pricing; the contract landman assembles the chain; the attorney interprets legal effect; the tax accountant controls basis and reporting. That allocation keeps the canonical four-person pod from treating clerical extraction as a substitute for a title opinion.

Apply jurisdictional rules to the property and the activity separately. Texas Occupations Code Section 1101.005 contains an exemption concerning dealings in mineral leases or interests, but its text does not create a nationwide license or authorize unrelated surface brokerage. For Oklahoma transactions, have local counsel classify the exact service under that state's licensing statutes before promising a procurement fee. Oklahoma forced pooling under 52 O.S. Section 87.1 creates order-specific elections and deadlines; a hearing notice is neither a completed well nor an assured royalty payment. North Dakota's dormant mineral framework, Chapter 38-18.1, requires analysis of statutory use, notice, and preservation procedures. Louisiana mineral servitudes raise prescription questions under Mineral Code Article 27 and related provisions, rather than a universal perpetual-severance assumption. Federal and Indian leases introduce additional agency requirements: 30 CFR Part 1206 governs valuation for covered production, not every private royalty check. Record property location, owner location, contact location, and the operator's service location because each can matter differently. For docket curve-jumping, archive the signed order and subsequent amendments, then separate legal status from engineering probability. Never label a proposed unit as producing merely because Enverus displays nearby completed wells. The landman should reconcile vendor records against the commission docket and county instruments before the acquisition model changes.

Separate buying assets for the firm's own account from selling interests or arranging investments for others. Securities Act Section 2(a)(1), 15 U.S.C. Section 77b(a)(1), expressly includes fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its securities definition. Entity interests and managed royalty pools can also raise investment-contract issues based on their actual structure. Before collecting investor commitments, have securities counsel identify the instrument, offering exemption, solicitation method, investor eligibility, state notices, and intermediary compensation. Rule 506(b) and Rule 506(c) are different operating paths: broad advertising does not fit the former, while the latter requires reasonable steps to verify accredited status and sales only to accredited investors. An exempt offering does not erase antifraud duties or resolve broker-registration questions under Exchange Act Section 15(a). A percentage of capital raised is a serious classification issue, not an administrative introduction fee. Keep institutional asset-sale outreach distinct from investor solicitation, and avoid publishing yield packages while assuming the transaction is merely a deed sale. For the four-person pod, the title attorney should identify when separate securities expertise is required and obtain it before marketing. If that expertise exceeds the approved contractor budget, remain an own-account buyer rather than improvising a pooled offering.

callout.title: Four Checks That Experienced Mineral Buyers Perform Early
callout.body: Spend specialist time where an apparently small drafting or docket detail changes the purchased cash flow.
items: Compare every NPRI fraction with both the reservation instrument and current lease; build fixed and floating interpretations before counsel selects the supported treatment.
Download pooling orders and amendments directly from the commission record; vendor status labels can lag changed election terms or dismissed proceedings.
Ask the payor whether suspense attaches to the owner account, a specific property, or a disputed fraction; those problems require different cures.
Obtain the institutional buyer's required title package before buying; a cheap tract can become unsalable when the eventual buyer requires expensive missing probate work.

sections.heading: 2. Write Contracts Around the Interest and the Payment Trigger
paragraphs: Use separate documents for acquisition, specialist services, and disposition. The purchase agreement should identify the exact estate, legal description, depth limitations, owned fraction, associated leases, and excluded rights. Attach a schedule rather than relying on a county name and a seller's spreadsheet. Specify whether the transaction covers mineral ownership, an NPRI, an overriding royalty, or another defined interest; those assets do not convey identical rights. State the price allocation, deposit handling, effective date, closing conditions, and treatment of receipts spanning that date. A per-NMA price needs an agreed net mineral acre definition and a title-adjustment mechanism; an NPRI purchase needs a separately defined economic fraction rather than an unexplained acre conversion. Include a title-defect notice period, defect valuation method, cure rights, minimum deliverable interest, and termination mechanics. Address probate, spousal signatures, entity authority, liens, and third-party consents where relevant. Texas Property Code Section 5.151 imposes a prescribed disclosure for covered mailed mineral purchase packages; use its current wording and format when the transaction falls within the statute. Do not substitute a friendly cover letter for required text. Record the final conveyance promptly and confirm indexing, because an executed deed sitting in email does not complete the recording work.

For the landman, define scope as specified counties, instruments, ownership questions, deliverables, and completion dates. For royalty reconciliation, define the properties, production months, source statements, exception thresholds, and allowed payor contacts. A service agreement should distinguish document collection from title interpretation and distinguish arithmetic exceptions from an asserted legal claim. Use fixed milestones or approved hourly budgets where suitable. If compensation depends on a closing or recovery, describe the exact trigger, calculation base, deductions, receipt date, reversals, and dispute process, then obtain the relevant licensing and professional-conduct analysis. Never pay on total sale proceeds when the agreed trigger is realized gain. Narrow anti-circumvention to identified counterparties, documented introductions, a reasonable term, and an express preexisting-relationship exception. It should not capture every mineral owner in a basin. Set a negotiated liability cap for appropriate service risks, with deliberate treatment of fraud, intentional misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and unauthorized transfers. Avoid assuming a cap can defeat nonwaivable statutory remedies. Define escalation, governing law, forum, and whether arbitration covers service disputes; local real-property proceedings may require different treatment. The principal approves budgets and business terms, while counsel drafts enforceable allocations rather than importing a software consulting form into a deed transaction.

Own the transaction evidence without claiming ownership of every underlying record. County instruments remain public records; vendor databases, imagery, and extracted datasets may carry contractual reuse restrictions. The service agreement should allocate ownership of newly prepared schedules and models, license necessary preexisting tools, identify permitted recipients, and require return or deletion of confidential seller materials when work ends. Check Enverus and county-access terms before placing exports in an institutional data room. For the flip, disclose the actual acquired interest, title exceptions, lease burdens, suspense status, and the provenance of production assumptions. A permit, drilling application, or pooling order cannot support a representation that reserves are proved. Match assignment language and warranty scope to what the seller can actually support. Obtain a closing statement separating consideration, transferred basis, expenses, and retained receivables. If purchase cost is $100,000 and gross disposition consideration is $130,000, the rights-trading gain before transaction costs is $30,000; the $100,000 returned basis is not operator revenue. Prevent duplicate recognition when accrued royalties are included in the purchase adjustment. Store the signed agreement, deed, recording receipt, funds confirmation, and accounting bridge together. The accountant should trace each recognized dollar to a royalty receipt or realized trading gain, not to a purchase price headline.

callout.body: The principal records these checks separately; one completed check does not substitute for the others.
items: Counsel confirms the purchased estate, fraction, authority to convey, material title exceptions, and required state-specific offer language.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Statutory Payment Rules with the Four-Person Pod
paragraphs: Royalty reconciliation begins with the lease and the payor's source data, not a blanket assumption that every deduction is improper. Obtain check detail, production month, sales volumes, realized prices, decimal interest, taxes, deductions, and prior-period adjustments. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 governs payment timing and specified withholding circumstances; Section 91.403 addresses interest. Oklahoma's Production Revenue Standards Act, including 52 O.S. Section 570.10, has its own payment and interest structure. Have counsel determine the applicable deadline, title condition, exceptions, and interest treatment before sending a demand. A division order helps administer payment but does not replace the underlying conveyance or lease; Texas Section 91.402 also restricts its effect on lease terms. Calculate a simple unit decimal only when the governing instruments support that method. Forty NMA in a 640-acre unit at a one-fifth lease royalty yields 0.0125 before applicable burdens or other allocation adjustments. Do not reuse that formula for a fixed NPRI, allocation well, or depth-limited interest without reviewing the operative documents. Flag volume discrepancies against state production records, recognizing reporting lags and differences between well production and sales. Escalate supported exceptions with a property identifier, production period, expected amount, observed amount, and documentary basis.

Keep taxes and management economics in separate but reconciled schedules. Internal Revenue Code Sections 611, 612, and 613A address depletion, basis, and oil-and-gas-specific limitations; eligibility depends on the taxpayer and interest, not a universal percentage applied to every deposit. The accountant should distinguish royalty income, acquisition basis, sale proceeds, realized gain, allowable deductions, and applicable state obligations. State severance taxes, local property taxes, and information reporting need their own calendars. A payor's tax deduction does not prove every owner filing has been completed. Preserve the canonical scorecard without replacing it with a transaction's headline proceeds: Conservative recognized revenue is $30,000, net margin is 20%, and owner net profit is $6,000. Base recognized revenue is $215,000, margin is 32.5%, and owner net profit is $69,875. Scaled recognized revenue is $400,000, margin is 45%, and owner net profit is $180,000. The corresponding differences between revenue and profit are $24,000, $145,125, and $220,000. These are scenario expense envelopes, not permission to expense returned acquisition principal as recurring overhead. Maintain a separate capital ledger for the $15,000 to $75,000 startup capital range. Explain timing and classification differences between cash movement, asset basis, and recognized results before comparing a quarter with the annual model.

Operate the Conservative and Base cases with one full-time principal and three contractors: landman, attorney, and tax accountant. The principal handles acquisition pricing, owner conversations, payment authorization, and institutional buyer relationships. The landman maintains tract-level evidence and monitors relevant commission dockets. The attorney reviews title, operative clauses, and jurisdictional questions within the retained scope. The accountant reconciles receipts, basis, and taxes. Use Airtable for tract and deadline tracking, QuickBooks for transaction accounting, and restricted document storage for source instruments; software does not decide title or waive contract deadlines. Automate royalty statement ingestion and production-change alerts, then route exceptions to the responsible person. For pooling-docket curve-jumping, require a second human check of order status and election dates before changing the bid. For NPRI acquisitions, require counsel's fraction interpretation before the model is released to a buyer. For institutional flips, assemble the buyer-ready evidence package before marketing. The Scaled case adds a second full-time operations analyst and a fourth contractor, such as a petroleum engineer, reaching six people rather than silently expanding the Base pod. With a six-to-twenty-four-month first-deal horizon and monthly operating expense range of $1,000 to $12,000, preserve capacity by rejecting unresolved low-value files early instead of multiplying speculative research assignments.

sections.heading: 4. Use Verbatim Outreach That States Role, Limits, and Next Steps
paragraphs: Use a plain initial owner-contact script: 'Hello, I am the principal of a business that buys mineral and royalty interests for its own account. Public records suggest you may own an interest in the tract described below. Those records can be incomplete, so I am asking whether you are the appropriate person to contact. We are interested in discussing a purchase, not collecting a fee from you. You do not need to send identification documents or bank details to have an initial conversation. If you prefer no further contact, reply stop and we will remove you from our outreach list.' Insert only verified sender and tract details. Do not imply affiliation with a producing operator, county office, or another owner. For commercial email, assess 15 U.S.C. Section 7704 and implement accurate headers, a truthful subject, required identification, a valid physical postal address, and a working opt-out with timely suppression. Maintain source, contact date, channel, and suppression status. If enclosing a deed and payment in a covered Texas mailing, apply Section 5.151 separately; this introductory script is not its prescribed disclosure. Never disguise a purchase solicitation as a royalty statement or an urgent government notice, and never suggest that silence transfers ownership.

For discovery, say: 'Before discussing price, may I confirm whether you hold minerals, a royalty reservation, or an inherited interest? Do you have a deed reference, lease, or recent statement you are comfortable sharing through our secure document channel? Please remove bank and tax identifiers from an initial copy. Are there other owners, estate proceedings, liens, or existing sale agreements we should account for? We will review the documents and explain the interest our offer covers, the proposed price, and any title conditions. You may have your own attorney review the documents before deciding.' Record answers as owner statements pending verification, not established title facts. For calls and texts, classify the actual campaign under 47 U.S.C. Section 227 and 47 CFR Section 64.1200, including technology, message purpose, number type, and applicable state restrictions. An offer to purchase property is not automatically treated identically to every sales solicitation; obtain a campaign-specific determination instead of assuming either universal exemption or universal coverage. Use manual, individually reviewed contact as the initial operating method, honor stop requests, and check relevant calling restrictions. Before recording, evaluate the laws implicated by both participants' locations; California Penal Code Section 632 illustrates why confidential calls need specific recording analysis. Do not record while that analysis remains unresolved.

For an institutional flip, use: 'We own the interest identified in the attached schedule and are evaluating a sale. The package separates recorded ownership, current lease terms, historical receipts, title exceptions, and development assumptions. Any pending pooling or drilling activity is labeled by its actual docket status and date. If this fits your acquisition criteria, we can provide a restricted data room and discuss your title requirements before agreeing on a closing schedule.' Use that ownership statement only after acquisition is complete; otherwise disclose the actual contractual position and transfer restrictions. For reconciliation, say: 'We are reviewing payments on an interest our firm owns. Please confirm the decimal and explain the listed adjustments for these production months. Our attached schedule identifies the source documents and arithmetic differences; please identify any title or account condition affecting payment.' These scripts support the five plays without adding outside service fees to the canonical revenue model. Log every material representation and retain the version of the package actually sent. The principal handles consequential conversations; contractors receive only their assigned documents. If a prospect asks to invest rather than sell an asset, stop the asset-buying script and route the proposal for securities review before accepting money or sending projected distributions. Suppression requests follow the contact across future lists.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: automation improves evidence throughput, but capital, depletion, and title still control returns. This chapter maps five plays: NMA acquisitions, NPRI underwriting, pooling-docket positioning, royalty recovery, and institutional flips. A 1 FT + 3 C pod uses Python ingestion, source-linked LLM extraction, production alerts, and permissioned buyer distribution to target 70% repetitive-work reduction without delegating title conclusions or binding commitments. Canonical annual owner profits remain $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled; the Scaled case requires 2 FT + 4 C. Build the flywheel around verified exceptions and reusable diligence, not bulk owner solicitation. Every automated result needs provenance, a recovery path, and an accountable reviewer.

sections.heading: 1. Build one evidence pipeline for five mineral-rights plays
paragraphs: Start with five explicit work queues rather than five disconnected software products. NMA acquisitions convert severed mineral ownership into tract-level purchase candidates; NPRI underwriting separates royalty participation from executive and leasing rights; pooling-docket positioning identifies public procedural developments before underwriting assumptions become stale; royalty recovery reconciles contracted economics against actual payments; institutional flips package verified interests for repeat buyers. These are this chapter's five mapped plays, with production monitoring serving all five. The full-time principal owns investment decisions, seller relationships, and cash authorization. Three contractor seats cover land/title work, petroleum and royalty analysis, and automation operations; licensed counsel handles legal interpretation within the land/title service scope where required. Define contractor deliverables and availability explicitly, because three contractors do not equal three full-time employees. Use one shared asset identifier but separate tract, deed, lease, well, unit, interest, and payment entities. A well can cross multiple tracts, and a tract can participate in multiple units. Flattening those relationships into one spreadsheet row silently corrupts both royalty decimals and acquisition rankings. Begin in one county and one operator population so the pod learns source quirks before increasing geographic coverage. Require every opportunity to identify its primary play, evidence owner, and next human decision.

Implement ingestion with Python's urllib.request, csv, json, hashlib, sqlite3, decimal, and datetime modules. A scheduler retrieves licensed feeds, permitted public downloads, and owner-authorized statement exports; it never bypasses access controls or assumes a public webpage permits unlimited scraping. Enverus or an operator portal can be a source when the subscription permits the intended use, while Texas Railroad Commission downloads supply public production and regulatory observations. Store the original artifact, retrieval time, source URL, content hash, reporting period, and parser version before extraction. For PDF images, call a contracted OCR endpoint through HTTPS rather than pretending the standard library can reliably extract scanned deed text. Pass OCR text to an LLM with a constrained JSON schema requesting instrument number, parties, dates, legal description, fractions, reservations, and supporting page spans. Treat document text as evidence, never as executable instructions. Reject unexpected fields, oversized responses, invalid dates, and fractions without their original wording. Use Decimal for money and Fraction for recorded fractional interests; save the untouched expression alongside normalized values. Land review resolves ambiguous conveyancing language rather than letting a model manufacture a clean ownership percentage. Version accepted extractions so later corrections remain traceable to their source and reviewer.

Receive vendor webhooks through an HTTPS endpoint with vendor-prescribed signature verification, timestamp checks, replay protection, and an explicit payload-size limit. Acknowledge only after a transaction durably records the event; a worker then processes pending rows. Where signatures are unavailable, retrieve the authoritative object through an authenticated API before trusting the notification. Build an idempotency key from source, artifact hash, and event type, not simply the seller's name. Duplicate notices must not create duplicate owners, payments, or offers. Separate immutable source records from interpreted facts and investment hypotheses. For example, a recorded deed is a source, a reviewer-approved conveyed fraction is an interpretation, and expected horizontal development is a hypothesis. Link each fact to page coordinates or an exact source excerpt, and expose those links beside every proposed action. A probabilistic extraction score is useful for queue ordering but cannot establish marketable title. The automation contractor maintains schemas and retry behavior; the land contractor accepts ownership facts; the principal accepts economic assumptions. This separation lets the same evidence support seller qualification, payment disputes, and buyer diligence without repeatedly buying the same research or allowing one mistaken extraction to propagate invisibly through every play. Weekly sampling checks whether that separation remains intact.

callout.title: Preserve the details that experienced mineral buyers inspect first
callout.body: Speed comes from eliminating repeated evidence assembly, not from skipping instrument interpretation.
items: Store gross acres, conveyed mineral fraction, and resulting NMA separately; never label a normalized royalty acre calculation as NMA.
Capture fixed-versus-floating NPRI wording verbatim with the granting and reservation clauses, because isolated fractions can reverse the economic interpretation.
Resolve pooling notices by legal description and docket identifier; owner-name matching alone misses trusts, estates, and spelling variants.
Index suspense releases and prior-period adjustments separately from current production receipts so a catch-up check does not inflate the forward royalty curve.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile royalties and monitor production without inventing entitlement
paragraphs: Build royalty reconciliation around production month, product, well or allocation group, payor, owner account, and statement revision. Cash date alone cannot explain an operator payment. Ingest line-level volumes, price, gross sales, ownership decimal, taxes, deductions, and adjustments using a source-specific field dictionary. Some statements report property gross values while others already report the owner's share; multiplying an owner-level amount by the royalty decimal again understates revenue. For an illustrative lease with a reviewed 0.00125000 payment decimal, 10,000 barrels at $70 create $700,000 property gross sales and $875 owner gross entitlement before applicable charges. If permitted owner-level taxes and deductions total $95, the illustrative net is $780. The calculation is a test fixture, not an additional scorecard revenue stream. Compare the modeled decimal with the division order and reviewed lease or instrument analysis; none independently resolves every title issue. Texas Natural Resources Code Section 91.402 supplies payment timing rules and specified exceptions, so the queue must distinguish delayed remittance from title-related suspense before generating correspondence. Require the royalty analyst to attach statement lines, contractual support, and the reconciliation bridge to any proposed recovery request. Record disputed amounts separately until collected or otherwise recognized under the established accounting policy.

Production monitoring should detect changed evidence, not promise early knowledge of future drilling. Maintain separate dates for production month, filing date, retrieval date, and revision date. Texas Railroad Commission oil reporting can be lease-level, while other datasets use well-level records; never manufacture well precision by spreading lease volumes equally. Preserve API identifiers, operator changes, unit relationships, and allocation methods. A Python job compares the latest accepted series with its prior version, checks missing periods, and calculates rolling changes only across comparable units and products. Trigger review when volumes fall materially against a documented baseline, when a previously inactive interest receives production, or when reported production diverges from paid volumes beyond the expected payment lag. Thresholds should reflect asset history and reporting cadence rather than a universal percentage. The petroleum contractor distinguishes normal decline, downtime, workovers, reporting revisions, and allocation changes before updating the underwriting curve. Keep commodity price changes separate from physical depletion: a revenue increase can conceal falling production. Route confirmed findings into acquisition valuations, NPRI cash-flow models, recovery cases, and buyer updates, but preserve their observation dates so institutional buyers can reproduce the conclusion. Stale inputs should visibly reduce confidence rather than quietly inherit yesterday's accepted status.

For pooling-docket curve-jumping, monitor public applications, hearing settings, amendments, orders, and subsequent development evidence as distinct events. Oklahoma Corporation Commission proceedings and Texas Railroad Commission proceedings operate under different statutes and procedures; a generic pooling label is insufficient. Have the land/title contractor identify the governing jurisdiction, instrument, acreage, affected interests, and any election deadline from the actual documents. An application is not an order, an order is not a drilled well, and a permit is not a royalty payment. The principal may reprioritize research when a public event changes the opportunity set, but the system must not auto-submit elections, waive rights, or send binding acquisition terms. Track deadlines with both a normalized date and the source language, including service facts that affect the calculation. For a changed or withdrawn filing, invalidate dependent alerts and send a correction to internal recipients. The same event history becomes a buyer-facing diligence timeline only after review and permission checks. This is how public procedural information supports distribution without turning uncertain development assumptions into sales claims. Maintain a daily human review calendar for active deadlines even when automated monitoring appears healthy, and designate a backup reviewer before the primary contractor becomes unavailable.

sections.heading: 3. Prove the automation rate and price every exception
paragraphs: Measure the 70% target against repetitive-work minutes, not the percentage of records that touched an LLM. Establish a manual baseline separately for research collection, qualification preparation, diligence fulfillment, and acquisition-channel administration. An illustrative monthly pilot processes 1,000 tasks that previously required six minutes each, or 6,000 minutes. Suppose 800 tasks pass deterministic checks and 200 need six-minute exception handling. Sample 80 of the passed tasks for six-minute human reviews, then reserve 120 minutes for monitoring and maintenance. Retained work totals 1,200 plus 480 plus 120, or 1,800 minutes; the reduction is exactly 70%. Acquisition judgment, title conclusions, negotiations, and cash authorization remain outside this repetitive task denominator. Publish results by queue as well as in aggregate so easy document downloads cannot conceal poor royalty accuracy. Stratify samples across sources, parsers, interest types, and monetary exposure, and inspect every consequential output even when its preparatory extraction passed. Expand review when errors cluster. If exception handling takes twelve minutes rather than six, the same pilot retains 3,000 minutes and saves only 50%. That sensitivity makes exception design a more important investment than adding another model to an already fragile workflow.

Price model calls as explicit planning assumptions rather than current vendor quotations. Assume one run consumes 5,000 input tokens at $2 per million and 800 output tokens at $8 per million: model cost is $0.0164. Add $0.0100 for allocated OCR and transport, producing $0.0264 variable cost per run. Two runs per task across 1,000 tasks cost $52.80 monthly. Add $75 for scheduled hosting, storage, and monitoring, then value the pilot's thirty retained labor hours at an illustrative blended $60 hourly, or $1,800. Total monthly workflow cost becomes $1,927.80, equivalent to $1.9278 per completed task and $23,133.60 annually. Vendor and platform cost alone is $127.80 monthly; cheap tokens do not make exception labor disappear. This budget excludes acquisition capital, title projects outside the measured workflow, licensed data subscriptions, and transaction-specific counsel. Allocate those separately within the business case. Do not charge retained contractor labor twice if the same hours already sit in the operating budget. Cache accepted extraction results by artifact hash and parser version, cap retries, and route repeated failures to review. A second model call is useful only when it improves a measured error class.

Keep the canonical economics fixed while allocating the proposed workflow inside them. Conservative revenue is $30,000 with $24,000 implied total costs and $6,000 owner profit at 20%; Base revenue is $215,000 with $145,125 costs and $69,875 profit at 32.5%; Scaled revenue is $400,000 with $220,000 costs and $180,000 profit at 45%. The first two cases use 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C. These are annual business scenarios, not outputs generated by the illustrative token model. The pilot's $23,133.60 annual workflow allocation fits within Base costs but would consume almost the entire Conservative cost allowance, so that case needs a smaller workload and budget. Monthly operating overhead of $1,000–$12,000 is a separate planning range, not a substitute for total scenario costs. Startup capital remains $15,000–$75,000 and time to first deal remains 3–9 months. Revenue means royalty receipts plus realized rights-trading gains excluding returned basis; gross sale proceeds and underlying producer sales are different measures. Track depletion analysis under 26 U.S.C. Sections 611 and 613A separately from operational yield metrics, and have the tax preparer determine eligibility and treatment rather than letting the workflow infer deductions from a generic percentage.

sections.heading: 4. Turn verified work into distribution and recover cleanly from failures
paragraphs: Build the acquisition flywheel from reusable explanations of observed owner problems. A reviewed royalty discrepancy can become an anonymized statement-reading guide; a verified tract research process can become a county-specific diligence checklist; a production revision can become an educational example explaining reporting lag. Publish only aggregated or permissioned information, removing owner identifiers and confidential instrument annotations. Programmatic pages should add original utility: local source links, an explanation of NMA versus NPRI, reporting cadence, and a clear intake path. Do not generate thousands of nearly identical acreage pages or publish speculative ownership claims as facts. Use source-linked draft generation followed by the relevant contractor's review and the principal's publication decision. The traffic loop is article, useful calculator or checklist, voluntary owner inquiry, qualified evidence request, verified opportunity, and another permissioned educational asset. A shareable royalty reconciliation template can support referrals without exposing a user's uploaded statement or creating a public owner leaderboard. Measure qualified inquiries and verified opportunities per published asset rather than raw visits. These assets support NMA acquisitions, NPRI qualification, and royalty recovery while leaving docket positioning dependent on primary public records rather than attention metrics. Schedule updates when source procedures change, and retire pages whose operational guidance can no longer be verified.

For outbound distribution, separate owner acquisition from institutional buyer placement. Owner outreach should use verified contact provenance, restrained cadence, accurate identity, and a suppression list shared across campaigns. Commercial email must follow 15 U.S.C. Section 7704 requirements, including accurate routing information, nondeceptive subjects, required identification and address information, and functioning opt-out handling. Do not convert a purchased list into automated calling or texting without evaluating the distinct rules for those channels. Institutional buyers receive a reviewed teaser matched to explicit preferences for basin, interest type, check size, producing status, and evidence completeness. Release detailed documents through recipient-specific access with an expiration date and an access log. The loop is buyer feedback, improved qualification rules, better diligence packages, shorter clarification cycles, and more repeat buyer engagement. Treat referral incentives as a separate operating decision requiring review of transaction structure and applicable licensing rules. If outside capital is pooled, assess securities implications before soliciting investors; 15 U.S.C. Section 77b expressly addresses fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights within its securities definition. A productive asset story does not remove those questions. Distribution automation ranks recipients and drafts communications; the principal authorizes actual offers, releases, and material representations.

Make recovery visible enough that the four-person pod can operate through vendor outages without losing deadlines. Maintain pending, processing, accepted, rejected, and quarantined event states with attempt counts and last-error categories. Retry temporary network failures with bounded exponential backoff; quarantine schema changes, signature failures, contradictory fractions, and source access problems instead of retrying them indefinitely. If an LLM endpoint fails, continue deterministic CSV reconciliation and route scanned instruments to manual review. If a production feed stalls, label affected observations stale and stop automated valuation refreshes while retaining the last accepted version. If outbound delivery fails, reconcile provider delivery identifiers before resending so the same owner or buyer does not receive repeated messages. Back up the database and original artifacts, test restoration, and maintain a daily export of active deadlines and high-value exceptions. Assign a secondary reviewer for urgent title and docket questions; software availability cannot substitute for qualified coverage. Review the complete flywheel weekly: research throughput, exception age, correction rate, qualified inquiries, accepted buyer packages, collected royalties, and realized trading gains. Increase automation only where accepted evidence remains reproducible and retained labor actually falls. The objective is a smaller distance between reliable facts and authorized action, not a larger volume of unreviewed machine output.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, holds Rank #25 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 81/100: asset selection matters, but transferable evidence determines whether the owner can leave. This chapter maps five operating plays: producing NMA acquisitions, NPRI acquisitions, royalty reconciliation, pooling-docket curve-jumping, and institutional flips. Build one accountable full-time owner around three scoped contractors, then add an operations employee and transaction contractor only when recurring workload supports six people. Canonical annual owner profits remain $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled. Weekly scorecards connect title defects, payment suspense, depletion, concentration, and contractor rework to cash. Separate mineral asset value from any transferable operating-service earnings; clean records support a defensible premium, while speculative multiples and duplicated royalty value destroy negotiating credibility.

sections.heading: 1. Assign five mineral plays to accountable seats, not overlapping vendors
paragraphs: Treat the five mapped plays as separate work queues sharing one tract register: P1 producing net mineral acre acquisitions, P2 nonparticipating royalty interest acquisitions, P3 royalty reconciliation and recovery, P4 pooling-docket curve-jumping, and P5 institutional flips. P1 buys mineral ownership subject to the actual lease and burdens; P2 buys a defined royalty interest whose instrument determines participation and payment rights. Neither an acreage label nor a broker spreadsheet proves the payable decimal. P3 improves collections on owned interests rather than creating a second revenue stream from the same royalties. P4 buys before a documented development catalyst, without treating a docket filing as a drilling commitment. P5 realizes a sale gain after removing returned basis. The full-time owner controls acquisition limits, pricing, liquidity, and counterparty communication. Three contractors own title evidence, engineering and production surveillance, and royalty accounting respectively. Every record carries a play identifier, county, legal description, instrument reference, lease reference, interest type, purchase cohort, and accountable seat. A single property can support several workflows, but its revenue, cost basis, and reserves appear only once in consolidated reporting. That rule prevents an attractive acquisition dashboard from becoming a double-counted sale presentation.

Write each contractor statement of work around accepted artifacts, response times, and exception ownership. The title seat supplies the document chain, burden schedule, acreage calculation, and unresolved-defect register; retain qualified counsel within that engagement when a legal title opinion or instrument interpretation is required. The engineering seat maintains well identifiers, production vintages, decline assumptions, and development probabilities using regulator records and licensed Enverus exports where available. The royalty-accounting seat reconciles EnergyLink statements, bank receipts, operator deductions, suspense balances, and the general ledger. An illustrative Base budget reserves $24,000 annually for title work, $12,000 for engineering, and $18,000 for royalty accounting. Those $54,000 of contractor costs sit inside, not above, the canonical $145,125 expense envelope. Use capped hourly work for uncertain curative matters and fixed deliverable fees for repeatable statement processing; require written estimates before exceeding a task cap. Do not pay title reviewers for finding fewer defects or engineers for increasing reserves. Pay monthly for accepted work, require correction of contractor-caused errors without additional fees under the agreed scope, and track disputed invoices separately. These amounts are planning allocations, not quotes or evidence that three contractors provide full-time availability.

At Conservative scale, four people means one owner plus three fractional specialists, not four salaries. The $24,000 total annual expense envelope cannot absorb the illustrative Base contractor budget. Buy narrowly scoped reviews, batch low-risk administration, and decline acquisitions whose diligence cost overwhelms expected receipts. At Scaled size, add one full-time operations controller and one fractional transaction-data contractor, yielding 2 FT + 4 C. The controller owns close discipline, contractor acceptance, access permissions, and exception aging; the transaction contractor builds buyer files and manages document requests without deciding title sufficiency. The owner retains investment decisions and external commitments. Add these seats only after a thirteen-week workload log demonstrates recurring demand and a twelve-month expense forecast fits the $220,000 canonical Scaled envelope. Assign backup procedures before assigning more properties. Contractor agreements must address confidentiality, record return, security, and signed copyright transfers under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a) where copyright ownership is being transferred. A work-made-for-hire label alone is insufficient for many commissioned materials. Separately inventory vendor licenses: ownership of a custom model does not convey redistribution rights to licensed source data. Evaluate worker classification under the actual relationship and applicable federal and state tests, rather than relying on invoice format.

callout.title: Keep scarce specialist hours attached to mineral value
callout.body: A lean pod wins by routing evidence correctly before expensive review, not by asking every specialist to inspect every file.
items: Send title reviewers a county-indexed instrument packet and a precise disputed-decimal question; pay for interpretation rather than avoidable document hunting.
Group royalty exceptions by operator and deduction code so one supported dispute can resolve several properties without duplicating specialist effort.
Archive the pooling application, subsequent order, amendments, and hearing status separately; a calendar entry is not a final development authorization.
Keep NPRI language beside the decimal calculation, especially fixed-versus-floating royalty wording, so a buyer can reproduce the interpretation without interviewing the founder.

sections.heading: 2. Enforce a weekly scorecard that measures defects, timing, and concentration
paragraphs: Publish the scorecard every Monday using Friday's frozen evidence snapshot. The owner spends forty-five minutes reviewing exceptions, not listening to activity summaries. For P1 and P2, report screened opportunities, accepted title packets, acquisition dollars awaiting unresolved defects, and days from complete packet to investment decision. Count an accepted packet only when the legal description, ownership chain, burdens, and payable-interest calculation are reproducible. For P3, show statement coverage, unreconciled dollars, suspense aging, disputed deductions, and recovered cash actually received. For P4, measure docket freshness and the percentage of catalyst claims supported by dated primary records; never score staff on rumored rig arrivals. For P5, report complete buyer files, qualified bids, bid-to-close conversion, and realized gain after basis removal. A reasonable internal target is at least 98% statement-dollar coverage within five business days of receiving complete inputs, with every material exception assigned that week. Define materiality explicitly: investigate any title or decimal discrepancy regardless of amount, and any unexplained cash difference exceeding the greater of $25 or 0.5% of the statement. Smaller differences remain logged and are investigated when cumulative balances cross that threshold. Label these as operating targets, not historical achievements.

Make quality visible through denominators and rework costs. Contractor first-pass acceptance equals deliverables accepted without substantive correction divided by deliverables submitted during the same period. Track the trailing thirteen-week result alongside the current week so one easy assignment cannot disguise a failing process. Separate external dependency delays from contractor delays, but require dated requests and follow-ups before stopping the contractor clock. Title packets waiting for courthouse retrieval remain visible as blocked inventory; they do not disappear from cycle-time reporting. Reconcile engineering updates against state production records, recognizing publication lag and later revisions. Texas Railroad Commission data and Oklahoma Corporation Commission records provide operating evidence, while the applicable instrument and title work establish ownership. Have the owner or controller sample three completed files weekly, or all files when fewer than three close, and reproduce one decimal and one cash bridge independently. At Scaled size, the transaction contractor cannot self-certify the completeness of the buyer room. Repeated material errors trigger a documented correction plan, increased sampling, and reassignment if agreed milestones fail. Pay incentives for timely, independently accepted artifacts, never for booked but uncollected recoveries or unsupported increases in development probability.

Set a hard concentration ceiling of 25% for each material revenue counterparty group and each institutional buyer group, consolidating affiliates under common control. Measure royalty exposure using trailing twelve-month receipts and stressed forward twelve-month receipts; measure flip exposure using rolling realized trading gains and a separate receivable-at-risk schedule. Also cap positive outstanding receivable exposure to any group at 25% of total receivables when that denominator exists. A four-group portfolio is the mathematical minimum at equal weights, but five groups provide practical headroom against payment timing and commodity changes. Establish a 22% early-warning threshold and prohibit discretionary purchases or unsecured extensions that would breach 25%. Recognize startup reality: a first producing property may exceed the policy immediately. Record that breach honestly, keep incremental exposure frozen, and use staged acquisitions across unrelated payers rather than describing the portfolio as diversified. Existing breaches require a funded reduction plan; counterparties cannot be renamed to manufacture compliance with the cap. Track basin, operator, commodity, and purchaser separately because four payers can still depend on one operator or gathering system. If gains or receivables are zero, report dollar exposures directly instead of manufacturing a percentage from an unusable denominator.

sections.heading: 3. Build accrual and cohort books that reconcile to the canonical economics
paragraphs: Maintain three linked views: a cash receipts ledger, an accrual operating ledger, and a property-level investment basis register. QuickBooks Online or Xero can hold the general ledger, while a controlled PostgreSQL database or protected workbook holds tract, well, lease, and instrument relationships. Software does not decide the accounting policy. The royalty accountant records production-month estimates only when the amount is supportable under the adopted reporting framework, then reverses or true-ups estimates when statements arrive. Reconcile opening receivables plus recognized royalty revenue less receipts and adjustments to closing receivables. Preserve gross royalties, production taxes, transportation deductions, other lease-authorized charges, and net cash as separate fields; document the chosen revenue presentation rather than mixing gross and net statement formats. Texas Natural Resources Code section 91.402 supplies payment-timing requirements and exceptions for covered proceeds, so suspense analysis must distinguish a lawful withholding reason from a missing division-order follow-up. Never treat every aged balance as immediately collectible. The canonical scorecard uses royalty receipts and realized rights-trading gains, excluding returned basis; show an explicit bridge from accrual results to that receipt-based operating view instead of silently changing the scorecard's revenue definition.

Tag each acquisition by closing quarter, interest type, basin, seller, and acquisition thesis. Allocate purchase price and qualifying transaction costs across acquired interests using a documented, consistently applied method, with accounting review for depletion, impairment, and partial dispositions. Tax depletion under 26 U.S.C. sections 611 and 613A requires its own eligibility and limitation analysis; a tax deduction is not a substitute for tracking economic decline. Keep book, tax, and management basis differences visible. Consider an illustrative institutional flip that collects $300,000 and disposes of rights with $240,000 allocated management basis. The operating trading gain is $60,000 before separately presented selling costs, not $300,000 of scorecard revenue. Record those selling costs exactly once under the adopted presentation. If the sale includes retained royalties, allocate basis between transferred and retained interests before calculating the realized gain. Cohort reporting then shows acquisition cash deployed, cumulative royalty receipts, realized gains, remaining carrying amount, and independent value estimates separately. A rising portfolio estimate cannot fund contractor invoices and does not become realized trading revenue. P3 recoveries retain their original property and production-month identifiers so collecting an old underpayment does not masquerade as improved current well productivity.

Reconcile the annual cases with arithmetic that the owner and a buyer can repeat. Conservative revenue of $30,000 less $24,000 of scenario expenses yields $6,000 owner net profit and a 20% net margin. Base revenue of $215,000 less $145,125 yields $69,875 and 32.5%. Scaled revenue of $400,000 less $220,000 yields $180,000 and 45%. These are the canonical operating scenarios, not additional forecasts layered over acquisition principal. Their average monthly expense equivalents are $2,000, $12,093.75, and approximately $18,333.33 respectively. The published $1,000 to $12,000 monthly opex range is therefore insufficient to describe every cost in the larger scenario envelopes; identify the bridge explicitly rather than forcing expenses into that range. The supplied scorecard does not itemize the difference, so the controller must substantiate actual overhead, transaction expenses, and other cost classifications before presenting a detailed budget. Acquisition capital of $15,000 to $75,000 belongs in investment funding, not automatically in operating expense. Track liquidity separately because six to twenty-four months to a first deal can consume cash before royalties arrive. Do not label owner net profit as transferable EBITDA until owner labor, financing, taxes, and noncash charges have been reconciled.

sections.heading: 4. Sell reproducible cash flows, or retain a genuinely transferable cash cow
paragraphs: Value the owned minerals before discussing a business multiple. An institutional buyer typically underwrites property cash flows using commodity assumptions, differentials, deductions, taxes, decline curves, development timing, title quality, and a required return. Prepare producing-only and probability-weighted development cases, then show sensitivity to price, decline, and delayed first production. Pooling records support a development narrative but do not replace economic underwriting: Texas Natural Resources Code section 102.011 addresses pooling under specified conditions, not a universal entitlement to immediate drilling. Label every development assumption and retain its evidence date. For initial negotiating sensitivity, test asset prices at three, four, and five times normalized next-year net royalty cash, then require the property model to justify or reject each result. Those are illustrative screens, not observed market comparables or promised transaction multiples. A rapidly declining well may fail even the lowest screen, while longer-lived production and credible additional inventory can require a different valuation approach. Never apply these screens directly to the $69,875 Base owner profit: that figure includes operating overhead and potentially trading gains, whereas the asset denominator must isolate the specific cash flows being purchased.

A separate operating-company earnings multiple is appropriate only when independently transferable service or origination earnings actually exist. The canonical Mineral Rights revenue basis contains royalties and realized rights-trading gains, not an assumed third-party management fee business. Consequently, do not invent recurring service revenue to justify a second valuation layer. If documented contracts later create genuinely separate earnings, test an illustrative two-to-four-times normalized annual operating earnings range, deducting market replacement labor and excluding asset royalties already valued elsewhere. For the current five plays, institutional-flip gains deserve transaction and cohort analysis rather than automatic recurring treatment. Rebuild three years of gains where records exist, distinguish repeatable sourcing from commodity appreciation, and identify capital required to replenish inventory. Convert any enterprise-value discussion to equity proceeds by addressing debt, cash, working-capital adjustments, retained properties, selling expenses, and entity-specific liabilities. A premium should be demonstrated as fewer pricing deductions, faster verification, or stronger bids against the same modeled cash flows. It is not an extra turn awarded merely because files occupy a polished data room. Request indications from multiple qualified buyers using identical property assumptions and reconcile differing bid terms before comparing headline prices.

Build the buyer room while operating, not during exclusivity. Include recorded conveyances, lease and amendment chains, division orders, title exceptions, production histories, royalty statements, bank bridges, tax schedules, contractor agreements, and signed assignments for transferable copyrighted work. A division order helps document payment administration but does not replace the underlying ownership chain. Provide role-based access, exportable registers, and a documented process for removing contractor credentials. Test transferability through a thirty-day founder-absence drill: the controller or designated contractor runs reconciliation, identifies new docket events, and prepares the weekly exceptions without unrecorded founder knowledge. The owner still handles reserved investment decisions, but routine operations must survive unavailability. For a durable cash cow, retain the same controls and compare distributable cash after reserve replenishment with sale proceeds after costs; depletion makes indefinite flat distributions an unsafe default. If raising pooled outside capital, analyze whether the interests offered are securities under 15 U.S.C. section 77b(a)(1), which expressly includes specified fractional mineral interests, and determine the applicable offering path before solicitation. Neither a contractor network nor a mineral label removes that analysis. The exit-ready pod is therefore also the hold-ready pod: clear ownership, reproducible cash, controlled concentration, and replaceable daily execution.

callout.title: Verify four conditions before committing to an exit process
callout.body: Proceed with sale representations only when the evidence package supports ownership, earnings, transferability, and the proposed transaction structure.
items: Reproduce every material NMA or NPRI decimal from the controlling instruments, reconcile exceptions, and identify any necessary curative work or price reserve.
Tie the three canonical revenue and profit cases to their exact expense envelopes; separate returned basis, acquisition capital, and accrual timing adjustments.

chapters.pull_quote: A mineral book earns a stronger bid when the next owner can reproduce every decimal, dollar, and decision without the founder.
action_checklist: Assign P1 producing NMA acquisitions, P2 NPRI acquisitions, P3 royalty reconciliation, P4 pooling-docket curve-jumping, and P5 institutional flips to named seats in one property register.
Execute three fractional-contractor scopes with capped fees, accepted artifacts, correction duties, response times, confidentiality terms, and signed copyright transfers where required.

Publish Monday scorecards from frozen Friday records, including title acceptance, reconciliation coverage, suspense aging, catalyst evidence, realized gains, and affiliated-counterparty concentration.
Reconcile $30,000, $215,000, and $400,000 of canonical annual revenue to $6,000, $69,875, and $180,000 of owner profit without treating returned basis as revenue.

Build separate producing-asset, contingent-development, and realized-trading-gain schedules; test illustrative valuation sensitivities without duplicating royalty value in an operating-company multiple.
Complete a thirty-day founder-absence drill and verify export permissions, buyer-room evidence, concentration reduction plans, and the expense capacity for any move to 2 FT + 4 C.

statutory_citations.title: 17 U.S.C. section 204(a) — Execution of transfers of copyright ownership
statutory_citations.relevance: A transfer of copyright ownership generally requires a signed writing; contractor-created models and documentation need appropriate executed assignments when ownership is intended to transfer.

statutory_citations.title: Texas Natural Resources Code section 91.402 — Time for payment of proceeds
statutory_citations.relevance: Sets payment-timing requirements and specified withholding circumstances for covered oil and gas proceeds, informing suspense aging and royalty collection escalation.

statutory_citations.title: Texas Natural Resources Code section 102.011 — Establishment of pooled unit
statutory_citations.relevance: Provides statutory conditions for Commission pooling action; docket-based acquisition underwriting must distinguish the relevant proceeding from a commitment to drill or a universal pooling entitlement.

statutory_citations.title: 26 U.S.C. section 611 — Allowance of deduction for depletion
statutory_citations.relevance: Establishes the federal depletion deduction framework, requiring property records that distinguish tax treatment from book expense and economic decline.

statutory_citations.title: 26 U.S.C. section 613A — Limitations on percentage depletion in case of oil and gas wells
statutory_citations.relevance: Contains oil and gas percentage-depletion restrictions and exceptions; eligibility and limitations require separate tax schedules rather than an automatic percentage applied to all royalty receipts.

statutory_citations.title: 15 U.S.C. section 77b(a)(1) — Definition of security
statutory_citations.relevance: The statutory definition includes investment contracts and fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights; pooled capital and offered interests require transaction-specific securities analysis.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #7, Mineral Rights, ranks #25 with a 81/100 Money-to-Manpower Score because title work, capital intensity, and depletion resist effortless scaling. This sprint operationalizes five mapped plays: producing NMA acquisitions, NPRI acquisitions, pooling-docket curve-jumping, owned-asset royalty reconciliation, and institutional flips. One full-time operator and three fractional contractors build an auditable acquisition pipeline rather than force a closing inside thirty days. Cap initial operating burn at $6,000, preserve acquisition reserves, and evaluate documented evidence at Days 30, 60, and 90. Canonical annual owner profits remain $6,000 Conservative, $69,875 Base, and $180,000 Scaled; none is a thirty-day receipt target. Scale verified underwriting capacity only after title, downside pricing, and buyer-depth thresholds pass.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Define Five Plays, Fund the Pod, and Freeze the Denominators
paragraphs: Launch one county and one producing formation, not a national mineral-buying campaign. For this chapter, the five mapped operator plays are P1, producing net mineral acre acquisitions; P2, nonparticipating royalty interest acquisitions; P3, pooling-docket curve-jumping; P4, reconciliation of royalties on owned interests; and P5, institutional flips. These are operating lanes within Candidate #7, not five independent businesses requiring separate staff. The full-time principal owns sourcing, cash authorization, underwriting version control, and buyer relationships. Three fractional contractors provide land and title research, reservoir or production analysis, and jurisdiction-specific legal review. Give each contractor a bounded deliverable rather than an unlimited research mandate. P1 and P2 establish what is being purchased; P3 changes the timing hypothesis; P4 tests whether ownership becomes collectible cash; P5 tests whether another buyer values the same evidence. Start with Oklahoma if pooling orders are central, using Oklahoma Corporation Commission records and the relevant county clerk. Do not transfer Oklahoma election mechanics into a Texas file. By Day 1, publish one responsibility sheet identifying the decision owner, authorized spend, required evidence, and escalation path for every lane. That sheet keeps a four-person pod from becoming four disconnected research queues.

On Days 2 and 3, separate the acquisition account from the operating account and impose a $6,000 first-month cash-burn ceiling. An illustrative allocation buys fifteen landman hours at $150, eight engineering hours at $175, four attorney hours at $250, $450 of records and data, $150 of outreach, and $750 of contingency: exactly $6,000. These are purchasing assumptions, not market quotations. The principal contributes the full-time seat; this launch budget excludes their draw and does not redefine annual owner profit. Four legal hours buy issue spotting and document scoping, not an unlimited title opinion. Any closing-specific work needs a separate written estimate before commitment. Candidate #7 requires $15,000–$75,000 of startup capital and has a stated $1,000–$12,000 monthly operating range; the sprint ceiling is a chosen control inside that range. After any purchase, retain six months of the approved operating budget in liquid cash, initially $36,000. Limit the first acquisition to 25% of committed equity, including its closing costs. Unfunded investor conversations do not count as committed equity. Maintain an additional asset-specific reserve for documented taxes, title work, and transaction obligations rather than spending the operating reserve twice.

Days 4 through 7 establish measurement before outreach creates a flattering pipeline. A screened tract is a unique legal description with a documented owner hypothesis, interest type, source date, and target formation. A verified file has every critical ownership, burden, acreage, and payment field supported, plus at least 90% completion of the remaining evidence checklist. Duplicate owners across mailing lists never create additional screened tracts. Separate gross acres, net mineral acres, royalty fractions, and decimal revenue interests in the database. An undivided 25% mineral interest across 160 gross acres equals 40 NMA. Under a simple uniform 640-acre unit with a 20% lease royalty, that interest would yield a 0.0125 revenue decimal: 40 divided by 640 multiplied by 0.20. Actual allocation can differ with tract participation, depth limitations, lease burdens, and horizontal allocation terms. An NPRI must be interpreted from its granting language rather than forced through this NMA calculation. Build these fields in Airtable or a controlled spreadsheet, attach instrument images, and assign immutable tract identifiers. End the week with twenty screened tracts, two contractor-reviewed examples, and a defect log that distinguishes missing evidence from evidence contradicting the seller.

callout.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Paying for Deeper Diligence
callout.body: A cheap interest with an unbounded research problem is not a cheap acquisition. Apply these checks before releasing the next contractor assignment.
items: Verify committed equity in the cash ledger; preserve $36,000 of initial operating reserves plus separately estimated asset obligations.
Require a county instrument trail connecting the proposed seller to the exact interest, depths, and legal description under review.
Independently recompute NMA and revenue decimals; send ambiguous fixed-versus-floating NPRI language to the attorney before pricing.
Obtain written contractor scopes within the $6,000 monthly ceiling; stop assignments that would consume unapproved closing-work budgets.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Turn County Evidence and Pooling Dockets into Priced Files
paragraphs: Day 8 begins with the recorded chain, not a broker's acreage summary. Retrieve the mineral deed, reservations, relevant leases, probate instruments, assignments, and recorded releases needed to establish the proposed conveyance. The landman identifies gaps; the attorney determines the legal effect of ambiguous grants and state-specific curative requirements. Treat an NPRI described as a fraction of royalty differently from a fixed fraction of production, and document whether the holder has executive rights or other associated rights. On Day 9, request available division orders, check detail, tax statements, and lease amendments from an authorized seller. A payor's decimal is corroborating evidence, not a substitute for title. Under 52 O.S. § 570.10, Oklahoma production-proceeds timing and interest provisions make payment dates and title-related suspense material underwriting inputs. They do not make every suspended balance immediately collectible. Record the payor's stated suspense reason, the documents requested, and the person responsible for curing it. Files with unresolved critical ownership facts remain outside the verified count even when the seller supplies attractive check stubs. By Day 10, four files should support reproducible ownership calculations and a specific list of remaining defects.

Use Days 10 and 11 to test P3 without mistaking regulatory activity for cash flow. Oklahoma's forced-pooling framework under 52 O.S. § 87.1 makes the application, notice record, hearing, final order, election terms, and subsequent filings distinct evidence events. Track them separately in the docket register. The operative order determines the relevant election requirements; never substitute a remembered statewide deadline for the actual document. Match the applicant, section-township-range description, targeted formations, and respondents against the acquisition file. Then check operator history, nearby completions, production reporting, and the evidence for development timing. A hearing date is neither a drilling commitment nor proof that capital has been allocated. Curve-jumping means buying a correctly identified interest before the market fully incorporates documented development evidence, not claiming confidential knowledge of an operator's plans. Preserve the timestamp of each public observation so a later buyer can reconstruct the thesis. Ask the engineer to state what event would invalidate the production assumption: canceled development, inferior offset performance, changed spacing, or uneconomic commodity prices. If the interest works only with an immediate new well, classify it as development exposure and do not price it as an established producing royalty.

Days 12 through 14 produce an illustrative price discipline independent of the canonical business scorecard. Model existing production monthly, using lease-specific net pricing, reasonable decline, documented deductions, production taxes, and an explicit terminal assumption. For a training case, use $65 oil and $3 gas as reference prices, then stress $45 oil, $2 gas, a 20% volume reduction, and six months of payment delay. These are chosen sensitivities, not current quotations or forecasts. Discount stressed net asset receipts at 10% annually using monthly timing, and cap all-in acquisition cost at 80% of that present value. A $60,000 stressed present value therefore supports at most $48,000 of purchase price plus closing costs combined. Exclude speculative wells from this initial hurdle; display development upside separately. Also calculate portfolio operating coverage as stressed next-twelve-month royalty receipts divided by approved next-twelve-month operating cash costs. Require at least 1.25 times coverage before claiming the owned portfolio supports its operating platform. A pre-acquisition sprint instead relies on funded reserves and cannot claim that status. Finish the week with six verified files, two reproducible stressed models, and a ranked queue that explains why rejected interests failed.

callout.title: Four Mineral-Desk Tactics That Save Real Diligence Dollars
callout.body: The best early advantage is preventing attractive-looking documents from becoming unsupported valuation assumptions.
items: Read NPRI granting language before using a broker's royalty-acre figure; fixed and floating fractions can create materially different receipts.
Save the actual pooling order beside its docket entry; calendar elections from the operative text and record who owns the response.
Compare production month with payment month before estimating decline; delayed checks can mimic falling production or exaggerate a rebound.
Ask institutional buyers for written county, depth, minimum-size, and title-package preferences before paying to assemble a portfolio they cannot purchase.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Test Sellers, Reconcile Royalties, and Establish Buyer Depth
paragraphs: On Day 15, contact owners through a documented, narrowly targeted process using verified addresses and a plain description of the interest sought. Use a letter or individually reviewed email rather than buying scale before ownership data works. Commercial email must satisfy applicable requirements of 15 U.S.C. § 7704, including accurate routing information, required identification, a postal address, and an effective opt-out mechanism. Telephone campaigns introduce separate rules and should not be added casually to this sprint. Record delivered contacts, substantive responses, document permissions, and seller price expectations as separate fields. A response is substantive only when the owner confirms the interest, supplies relevant evidence, or discusses terms; automated replies do not count. On Day 16, compare asking prices with the stressed all-in ceiling before commissioning additional work. Any indication of interest should state the precise property scope, diligence conditions, cost assumptions, and expiration mechanics drafted for the transaction. Do not send an accidentally binding purchase commitment from a spreadsheet template. By Day 17, the attorney should categorize curative tasks by responsible party, expected expense, and dependency. Stop a file when the seller refuses necessary evidence or insists on an interest the recorded instruments do not support.

Days 18 and 19 test P4 with an owned interest or a seller-authorized diligence sample. The latter produces an underwriting finding, not operator revenue. Reconcile each payment line using property identifier, production month, product, reported sales volume, realized price, ownership decimal, deductions, taxes, and payment date. Maintain separate columns for gross well sales and the interest holder's receipts. For example, $80,000 of gross sales multiplied by a 0.0125 decimal produces $1,000 before attributable deductions and taxes; it does not produce $80,000 of operator revenue. Route differences exceeding the greater of $25 or 2% of expected net receipts into an exception queue. That threshold prioritizes research rather than waiving smaller contractual amounts. Categorize each difference as timing, decimal, pricing, deduction, tax, or missing production evidence. Use Python csv and decimal modules or a controlled spreadsheet to automate matching, while retaining original statements and human-reviewed exceptions. Production monitoring should alert on a 20% unexplained change across comparable months, not declare a reservoir problem from one late report. P4 earns its place by reducing leakage and improving asset knowledge; unresolved recovery claims stay outside receipts until actually collected under the chosen operating scorecard convention.

Days 20 and 21 test P5 before assuming an institutional exit. Obtain two written buyer responses specifying county, formation or depth, interest type, minimum package size, required title evidence, and valuation method. These responses establish buyer fit, not a committed bid. Share a redacted teaser first and release seller-authorized documents through a controlled data room only when their use is permitted. Calculate net sale economics after transaction expenses and distinguish returned basis from recognized gain. Buying an interest for $40,000, capitalizing $2,000 of acquisition costs, and selling for $50,000 with $3,000 of selling expenses produces $5,000 of realized gain under this simplified illustration. The $42,000 recovered investment is not revenue. Track selling expenses once rather than subtracting them again in the operating ledger. If investors will pool money, stop fundraising until counsel determines the instrument, offering path, intermediary obligations, and required filings. The security definition in 15 U.S.C. § 77b(a)(1) expressly addresses fractional undivided interests in oil, gas, or other mineral rights; an entity wrapper does not settle the analysis. This sprint assumes funded principal equity and direct asset acquisition, avoiding dependence on an unfinished offering to meet purchase or operating commitments.
